title: Baker Mayfield on playing Browns: Ultimately, you remember the good more than the bad
summary: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield has had Sunday’s game circled since the schedule release in the spring, as Tampa Bay will host Cleveland — the team that drafted him No. 1 overall in 2018.
full_text: Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield has had Sunday’s game circled since the schedule release in the spring, as Tampa Bay will host Cleveland — the team that drafted him No. 1 overall in 2018. The end of Mayfield’s time with the Browns was ugly, with the team eventually replacing him with Deshaun Watson after an injury-plagued 2021. But in 2020, Mayfield helped the club end a long postseason victory drought with a blowout win over the division-rival Steelers in the wild card round. Asked how he remembers his time with Cleveland, Mayfield emphasized the positive. “Yeah, I mean, with any experience, there’s ups and downs, good and bad. Ultimately, you remember the good more so than the bad ,” Mayfield said. “Yeah, first time having a playoff win since ’94 there. And going on the road and doing it in Pittsburgh. “So, a lot of good memories there. A lot of teammates that are friends for life. But like I said earlier, it’s a very different building now.” Different coaching staff or not, Mayfield is known for playing with his emotions on his proverbial sleeve and a chip on his shoulder. To combat some of the potential ill effects of that, Mayfield said he’s focusing on making sure he gets the little things right this week, particularly after fumbling three times in the Week 1 loss to Cincinnati. “Taking it one day at a time, making sure that you harp on little details,” Mayfield said. “That goes back to, obviously, not coming out on the right side of the game last week, of really focusing on the small details. And so, when you do that, good things will happen on Sundays. “So, for me, focusing on that and then when the lights come on, you get out there and play, it’s time to go — let it loose.”
author: Myles Simmons

title: Former All-Pro LB Fredd Young dies at 64
summary: Fredd Young, a member of the list of the top 50 Seahawks players in franchise history, has died.
full_text: Fredd Young, a member of the list of the top 50 Seahawks players in franchise history, has died . He was 64. Seattle made Young the 76th overall pick in the 1984 draft. He played college football at New Mexico State. Young made the Pro Bowl from 1984 through 1987, and he was an AP first-team All-Pro in his fourth and final season with the Seahawks. As a rookie, he became the first AFC player to make the Pro Bowl as a special-teams player who wasn't a return specialist. In 1988, Young was traded to the Colts for a pair of first-round picks after a contract fight with the Seahawks. He then spent three seasons in Indianapolis. For his career, Young appeared in 101 regular-season games with 79 starts.
author: Mike Florio

title: Travis Kelce was a victim in a Ponzi scheme
summary: Two years after Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce was the direct victim of thievery via a burglary at his home, it has come to light that he was robbed in a different way.
full_text: Two years after Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce was the direct victim of thievery via a burglary at his home , it has come to light that he was robbed in a different way. Via TMZ, Kelce was named in court on Tuesday as one of the victims of Siddarth Jawahar, who bilked investors out of more than $35 million. Jawahar was sentenced to 11 years in prison and ordered to pay more than $31 million in restitution. Kelce's losses weren't disclosed. Per prosecutors, Siddarth initially funneled nearly all of his clients' funds into Philip Morris Pakistan. When that failed, he used money from new investors to pay existing investors. Kelce has made plenty of money, both on and off the field. (And he has married very well.) Whatever he lost, he'll be fine. Still, it's another reminder that, when a potential investment seems too good to be true, it probably is.
author: Mike Florio

title: Mike Vrabel: TreVeyon Henderson will increase practice workload on Wednesday
summary: There is some positive news on the injury front for one of New England's key young players.
full_text: There is some positive news on the injury front for one of New England's key young players. Head coach Mike Vrabel said in his Wednesday press conference that TreVeyon Henderson should do more at practice on Wednesday as he continues to recover from an ankle injury. Henderson did not play in the Week 1 loss to Seattle a week ago. He was on the field for Monday's practice in a limited capacity. "We'll continue to evaluate that and see where he is, and hopefully that continues to trend in the right direction ,” Vrabel said, via Doug Kyed of the Boston Herald. Henderson, a second-round pick in last year’s draft, accounted for 1,132 yards from scrimmage and 10 total touchdowns as a rookie. New England’s first injury report for the Week 2 matchup against Pittsburgh is due out later on Wednesday.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Giants expect Aaron Donald to play on Monday night
summary: Rams head coach Sean McVay said on Monday that the team has not decided whether defensive tackle Aaron Donald will play in Week 2, but the opposing head coach believes he knows the answer.
full_text: ' Rams head coach Sean McVay said on Monday that the team has not decided whether defensive tackle Aaron Donald will play in Week 2, but the opposing head coach believes he knows the answer. The Giants will be in Los Angeles for a Monday night game and head coach John Harbaugh said that the team believes Donald will be making his first appearance since coming out of retirement. "We are expecting him to play ," Harbaugh said, via Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post . "We are expecting him to be Aaron Donald. He’s a game-wrecker." 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan had the same expectation heading into last Thursday's game, but Donald did not travel to Australia with the Rams for the opener. Shanahan did have to contend with Myles Garrett, who was ineffective while trying to play through a knee injury that landed him on injured reserve this week. We'll likely find out closer to kickoff if Harbaugh and the Giants are going to have to deal with either one.
author: Josh Alper

title: Chiefs will have Mansoor Delane at Wednesday's practice
summary: Word on Tuesday was that Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane avoided a serious shoulder injury in Monday night's win over the Broncos and the first-round pick is set to be back on the field right away.
full_text: ' Word on Tuesday was that Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane avoided a serious shoulder injury in Monday night's win over the Broncos and the first-round pick is set to be back on the field right away. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid told reporters at a Wednesday press conference that Delane will take part in their first practice of the week. Delane intercepted Broncos quarterback Bo Nix on the third play on Monday night, but came down on his shoulder and did not return. Delane also dealt with a shoulder issue in the offseason. Reid said that offensive tackle Josh Simmons (back) and defensive back Chamarri Conner (knee) will remain out of practice. They were both inactive for the win over Denver. Linebacker Cooper McDonald (knee) will also miss practice and Reid said he will be placed on injured reserve.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nick Sirianni explains decision not to put Landon Dickerson on injury report
summary: Apparently, an injury isn't an injury if a team doesn't know with certainty what the injury is.
full_text: Apparently, an injury isn't an injury if a team doesn't know with certainty what the injury is. That's the story to which the Eagles are sticking, when it comes to the failure to put guard Landon Dickerson on the Week 1 injury report. Via Zack Berman of The Athletic , coach Nick Sirianni told reporters on Wednesday that Dickerson didn't appear on the report because the injury wasn't determined until imaging was conducted after the game . So is Sirianni saying the Eagles had no idea Dickerson was injured at all? "A few weeks ago, [I] got rolled up on in practice," Dickerson said Monday. "I thought as weeks went by it would get better. It didn’t, and we kind of went out there and finally got some imaging on it today, figured out what was wrong with it." Figuring out the specific injury seems to be different from knowing there's an injury. And while it's possible Dickerson kept it to himself, it's hard to imagine no one noticing that Dickerson wasn't 100 percent. The real question will be whether Dickerson received treatment from the team. There will be records of whether that happened. If it did. For now, all we know is that the Eagles (and Dickerson) didn't know what was wrong until they took a look at whatever is going on inside his knee.
author: Mike Florio

title: 49ers to put WR De'Zhaun Stribling on injured reserve
summary: 49ers rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling will miss at least four games due to the ankle injury he suffered in last Thursday's season-opening win over the Rams.
full_text: 49ers rookie wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling will miss at least four games due to the ankle injury he suffered in last Thursday's season-opening win over the Rams. Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that the 49ers will place Stribling on injured reserve. A report earlier this week indicated Stribling will not require surgery to repair the injury. Per a report from Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, the 49ers will sign wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge to their 53-man roster. Hodge was elevated from the practice squad in Week 1. Tight end Jake Tonges was also injured in the win and head coach Kyle Shanahan suggested he’d miss time as his MCL recovers, but the team has not moved him to injured reserve at this point.
author: Josh Alper

title: Deshaun Watson: The media thinks I'm supposed to throw for 400 yards, 5 TDs each week
summary: Deshaun Watson will start for the Browns again on Sunday when they play Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers.
full_text: Deshaun Watson will start for the Browns again on Sunday when they play Baker Mayfield and the Buccaneers. Fortunately for Watson — who was vociferously booed by Cleveland fans during the preseason — the start will come on the road. But Week 3 looms, which will be the Browns' home opener against the Panthers. Does Watson feel like he has to put up a solid performance this week to build up some goodwill with the fanbase? "No, I think personally, I think all that is for the media ," Watson said in his Wednesday press conference. "I think the media has this expectation that I’m supposed to throw [for] 400 yards and five touchdowns every week. So, until that happens, I guess it’s going to be the same situation. "Again, my job is to make sure I’m operating well so we can try to get a win and keep moving forward from there." And what did Watson see on film from the Week 1 loss to the Jaguars? "Finding completions, operating well. That’s pretty much it," Watson said of his performance. "Had one turnover, a couple — that one sack-fumble, have to protect the ball, but we recovered it. That’s pretty much it, for real. We just didn’t have opportunities in the red zone to get points. Only six incompletions — one of them was a pick, one of them was the end of the game, end of the half. Tipped ball. Two missed throws, and then a throwaway." It's hard to know what Watson means by operating well, as the offense finished with multiple pre-snap penalties and had to resort to a timeout to avoid more. It's also worth noting that when it comes to expectations for Watson, they are quite low — whether it's from the media or the fanbase. That's part of why Cleveland's fanbase is so frustrated, because the perception based on his performance over several years is that he gives the club little chance to win. Watson has not yet thrown for even 300 yards since joining the Browns. It’s unlikely Week 2 will be the first time that happens.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Falcons haven't made a QB choice for Week 2
summary: Head coach Kevin Stefanski said they are "not ruling anyone out" against the Panthers.
full_text: ' Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski did not name a starting quarterback for Week 2's home game against the Panthers at his Wednesday press conference. The Falcons started Cooper Rush for their opener after ruling Tua Tagovailoa and Michael Penix out against the Steelers. Stefanski said that Tagovailoa will not practice on Wednesday due to an oblique injury, but Rush will be on the field despite receiving treatment for his back along with Penix. Penix is returning from last season's torn ACL and has been cleared for full practice, but said last week that he does not feel all the way back from his injury yet. "We will have a quarterback for this week," Stefanski said. "Not yet, but we’ll work through that this week. . . . I’m not ruling anyone out.” After being asked about undrafted rookie Jack Strand later in the press conference, Stefanski confirmed that he has not been ruled out as a potential choice. Stefanski declined to say whether Penix is getting the kind of first-team work that would signal he's got the green light for game action, which suggests the likeliest choice for this week is another start for Rush. The Falcons would then move on to a Thursday night game in Green Bay before an extended break leading into Week 4.
author: Josh Alper

title: Evan McPherson wins fifth AFC special teams player of the week award
summary: The Bengals got a good week from their kicker and the league has recognized him for it.
full_text: The Bengals got a good week from their kicker and the league has recognized him for it. Evan McPherson has been named AFC special teams player of the week for his role in Cincinnati's 33-27 victory over Tampa Bay in Week 1. McPherson finished Sunday 4-of-4 on field goals, hitting from 20, 55, 58, and 32 yards. He was also 3-of-3 on extra points. McPherson was the only player to hit two field goals of at least 55 yards in Week 1. This is McPherson’s fifth special teams player of the week award. He last won it for Week 13 of the 2025 season.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Cardinals WR Simi Fehoko is the NFC special teams player of the week
summary: Wide receiver Simi Fehoko helped the Cardinals get their 2026 season off on the right foot.
full_text: Wide receiver Simi Fehoko helped the Cardinals get their 2026 season off on the right foot. Fehoko blocked a punt with the Cardinals up two points in the fourth quarter last Sunday and that play set up a touchdown that helped them on their way to a 26-14 win over the Chargers. The Chargers were the biggest favorites in the league heading into Week 1. Fehoko also had a tackle while covering a kick earlier in the game. He was named the NFC special teams player of the week on Wednesday. It's Fehoko's second season with the Cardinals. He had seven tackles while playing special teams last season.
author: Josh Alper

title: Zack Baun is the NFC defensive player of the week
summary: Eagles linebacker Zack Baun helped his team to a win in their season opener and he also received some individual accolades for his work against the Commanders.
full_text: Eagles linebacker Zack Baun helped his team to a win in their season opener and he also received some individual accolades for his work against the Commanders. Baun had 12 tackles and a tackle for loss in the 24-22 win. He also broke up a pair of passes thrown by Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels. The NFL announced on Wednesday that Baun has been named the NFC defensive player of the week in recognition of that effort. It's the second time that Baun has been awarded the prize. The other instance came during his first year in Philadelphia in 2024. Baun also made the All-Pro team that year and he's been a Pro Bowl selection in both of his years as an Eagle.
author: Josh Alper

title: T.J. Watt earns record-tying ninth AFC defensive player of the week award
summary: T.J.
full_text: '' T.J. Watt’s big game helped power the Steelers to victory on Sunday. Now he has been named AFC defensive player of the week. Watt recorded a 35-yard pick-six, three tackles for loss, and 2.0 sacks in Pittsburgh’s 20-13 victory over Atlanta in Week 1. It was Watt’s 10th career interception. He now joins Hall of Famer Julius Peppers as the only two players to record at least 100 sacks and 10 interceptions since 1982. Watt now has nine career defensive player of the week awards, which ties Hall of Famers Chris Doleman, Bruce Smith, and Lawrence Taylor for the most ever. This is his first DPOW award since 2024.
author: Myles Simmons

title: D'Andre Swift named the NFC offensive player of the week
summary: The Bears had the most impressive offensive performance of Week 1 and one of their players' contributions to it was recognized by the league on Wednesday.
full_text: ' The Bears had the most impressive offensive performance of Week 1 and one of their players' contributions to it was recognized by the league on Wednesday. Running back D'Andre Swift has been named the NFC offensive player of the week. Swift ran 18 times for 124 yards and three touchdowns during Chicago's 59-37 win over the Panthers. The three touchdowns are a single-game high for Swift, who also caught one pass for 10 yards during the win. It's the second time that Swift has taken offensive player of the week honors. He also earned the prize while playing for the Eagles in 2023.
author: Josh Alper

title: Kenneth Walker named AFC offensive player of the week
summary: Kenneth Walker had an outstanding debut for the Chiefs on Monday night and now the league has recognized him for the performance.
full_text: Kenneth Walker had an outstanding debut for the Chiefs on Monday night and now the league has recognized him for the performance. Walker has been named AFC offensive player of the week. Walker accounted for 191 yards from scrimmage — 173 rushing, 18 receiving — and two touchdowns as the Chiefs defeated the division-rival Broncos, 31-10. Walker’s 60-yard touchdown in the third quarter helped put the game firmly in Kansas City’s hands. The Super Bowl LX MVP, Walker now has two career player of the week awards. This is his first time winning a player of the week since 2023.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Steelers plan for Joey Porter Jr. to do more at practice Wednesday
summary: Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. appears to be moving closer to a return to the Steelers lineup.
full_text: Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. appears to be moving closer to a return to the Steelers lineup. Head coach Mike McCarthy said earlier this week that he hoped Porter would increase his practice work after missing last Sunday's win over the Falcons. Porter spent all of training camp on the physically unable to perform list and was limited in practice last week, but McCarthy indicated he could be a full participant on Wednesday. "Our plan is to move forward with Joey and see how much more he could do today," McCarthy said, via 93.7 The Fan. Porter was dealing with a back injury this summer, but he was also looking for a contract extension that did not come before Week 1. Porter has not committed to playing without a new deal and the Steelers have a policy of not negotiating during the season.
author: Josh Alper

title: NFL declines comment on whether Broncos tampered with Drew Brees
summary: With the Broncos seemingly concerned that their contact with Drew Brees prior to the AFC Championship could put them in a tampering jackpot, we decided to ask the league whether the specific situation runs afoul of the rules.
full_text: With the Broncos seemingly concerned that their contact with Drew Brees prior to the AFC Championship could put them in a tampering jackpot, we decided to ask the league whether the specific situation runs afoul of the rules. The NFL declined comment. It's not clear what that means. If it's a nothing burger, the league easily could have said so. The problem for the Broncos is that the NFL enforces the tampering rules unpredictably and sporadically. More often than not, the league looks the other way. During the days of rampant tampering in and around the Scouting Combine, the NFL rarely does anything about it. Sometimes, however, the NFL decides to make an example out of someone. In this case, the effort to feed ESPN an interesting story for the first Monday night pregame show of the season has also handed the league enough evidence to take action, if it chooses to do so. The only question remaining is whether the NFL will choose to do so. Again, it doesn't take a complaint from the team that holds a player's rights. The Dolphins were hammered for tampering with Sean Payton and Tom Brady, based on evidence the NFL tripped over during an unrelated investigation. Here, the evidence fell into the NFL's laps. Thanks to a report that pushed the idea that the Broncos contacted Brees at a time when he remained on the Saints' reserve-retired list.
author: Mike Florio

title: Falcons sign TE Nick Muse to 53-man roster, put DL Da'Shawn Hand on IR
summary: Falcons defensive lineman Da'Shawn Hand suffered a season-ending quad injury in the season opener and the Falcons moved him off the active roster on Wednesday.
full_text: ' Falcons defensive lineman Da'Shawn Hand suffered a season-ending quad injury in the season opener and the Falcons moved him off the active roster on Wednesday. Hand was placed on injured reserve and the Falcons announced that they have signed tight end Nick Muse off of their practice squad in a corresponding move. They also signed defensive end Drake Jackson and running back Khalil Herbert to the practice squad. Muse signed with the Falcons in August and joined the practice squad after being released as part of the final cuts. He was elevated from the practice squad for the team's Week 1 loss to the Steelers and made one tackle on special teams. Muse played in 16 games for the Vikings between 2022 and 2024. He caught one pass during his time in Minnesota.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cardinals to place S Kitan Crawford on IR
summary: The Cardinals will be without one of their young contributors for at least the next four weeks.
full_text: The Cardinals will be without one of their young contributors for at least the next four weeks. Per Ian Rapoport of NFL Network, Arizona is placing safety Kitan Crawford on injured reserve. Crawford was carted off the field during Sunday’s victory over the Chargers. He has a mid-ankle sprain and is expected to return during the season. Crawford played 14 special teams snaps and seven defensive snaps in Week 1. A seventh-round pick in the 2025 draft, Crawford appeared in 15 games with one start as a rookie last year, recording 20 total tackles and one pass defensed.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Joe Brady: No concerns about Highmark Stadium field for Thursday night
summary: The condition of the playing field at the new Highmark Stadium became a talking point after the Bills played their first preseason game at the building this summer.
full_text: ' The condition of the playing field at the new Highmark Stadium became a talking point after the Bills played their first preseason game at the building this summer. Some players aired concerns about the size and frequency of divots that came up during the course of play, which led the Bills to replace the field ahead of Thursday night's inaugural regular season game against the Lions. The Bills worked out at the stadium on Tuesday and head coach Joe Brady said that the team will not go into the game with reservations about the condition of the field. “I really don't have many concerns with it,” Brady said, via Jay Skurski of the Buffalo News . “There wasn't a lot of concerns with it the first go around with it in terms of there was stuff that was moving. I credit our leadership that I understand that they want to have the best surface out there and be able to make the decision and kind of go with it. But, yeah there’ll be no concerns come Thursday. Our guys are excited just to be on grass.” Linebacker Greg Rousseau agreed with Brady's closing statement and said he believes "it'll be smooth" based on Tuesday's experience. The Bills will be hoping that's the case so they can avoid the playing surface overshadowing anything about the game itself in the aftermath of the home opener.
author: Josh Alper

title: Colts LB Akeem Davis-Gaither will wear helmet transmitter this week
summary: The Colts are making a change to their defensive operations after getting blown out by the Ravens in Week 1.
full_text: The Colts are making a change to their defensive operations after getting blown out by the Ravens in Week 1. Head coach Shane Steichen said on Wednesday, via multiple reporters, that linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither will wear the helmet transmitter and relay defensive calls to the rest of the unit this week. Safety Cam Bynum wore the green dot for the Ravens game. The move comes a day after defensive coordinator Lou Anarumo said that the team was considering a change because of a number of communications breakdowns that helped the Ravens roll up 506 yards of offense in a 41-13 win. Davis-Gaither will be lined up in a more central spot on defense while Bynum was playing deeper in the secondary. The Colts will put the new system to the test in Kansas City on Sunday night.
author: Josh Alper

title: Josh Allen is first, Caleb Williams is second in MVP odds
summary: One week into the 2026 season, Bills quarterback Josh Allen remains the favorite to be named the NFL Most Valuable Player.
full_text: ' One week into the 2026 season, Bills quarterback Josh Allen remains the favorite to be named the NFL Most Valuable Player. But there's a new contender in second place. Bears quarterback Caleb Williams' odds have skyrocketed after his performance in Chicago's 59-37 Week 1 win at Carolina. Allen's odds improved from +600 to +500, while Williams is now just behind Allen at +600. Prior to Week 1, Williams was at +1200. The next-best odds belong to Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson at +650, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow at +900, 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy at +1200. Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes at +1600, Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott at +1800 and Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence at +1800. Last year's MVP, Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford, saw his odds drop to +2000 from his preseason odds of +1400 after the Rams' ugly Week 1 loss.
author: Michael David Smith

title: ESPN, Joe Buck strike new deal worth more than $100 million
summary: Fortunately for Joe Buck (and for ESPN), Disney doesn't apply the same rules the Steelers do to redoing contracts after football season has started.
full_text: Fortunately for Joe Buck (and for ESPN), Disney doesn't apply the same rules the Steelers do to redoing contracts after football season has started. Andrew Marchand of The Athletic reports that ESPN and Buck have agreed to a new deal that pays out more than $100 million. In all, the six-year extension is worth roughly $108 million. That's an average of $18 million per year. His current deal pays out $15 million annually. The contract runs through 2032, beyond the expiration of ESPN's current deal with the NFL. Which essentially confirms (as if there was any doubt) that ESPN will emerge from the coming game of broadcast-rights musical chairs with a seat at the table. As Marchand notes, Troy Aikman does not yet have a new deal. Buck and Aikman left Fox together for ESPN in 2022, and there were suggestions last month that they could be a package deal . Aikman's five-year, $90 million contract runs through the Super Bowl, which ESPN/ABC will televise. Aikman was already at $18 million per year. With Buck matching it, Aikman surely will be looking to get to at least $20 million. To go along with whatever he's currently getting as a consultant for the Dolphins.
author: Mike Florio

title: Todd Monken responds to Mike Tomlin: It's not Browns being Browns, it's Browns playing poorly for one week
summary: During the pregame show for Sunday night's matchup between the Cowboys and Giants, new NBC analyst Mike Tomlin quoted one of his former players when talking about Cleveland's ugly 34-10 loss to Jacksonville.
full_text: During the pregame show for Sunday night's matchup between the Cowboys and Giants, new NBC analyst Mike Tomlin quoted one of his former players when talking about Cleveland's ugly 34-10 loss to Jacksonville. "In the words of my friend JuJu Smith-Schuster," Tomlin said, "the Browns is the Browns." Smith-Schuster made those words famous back in 2020, ironically before the Browns then pounded the Tomlin-led Steelers in the wild card round. But the saying has stuck in part because the Browns have had just one winning season since — and even that ended with an ugly postseason loss. Asked about Tomlin’s comments in his Monday video conference, first-year head coach Todd Monken seemed to take some exception to them. “Well, again, everybody’s afforded their opinions. That’s what you do when you go from coaching to television,” Monken said. “ We have to own that . We have to own that. We didn’t play very well. I don’t see it that way, Browns being Browns. I don’t see it that way. Every week is different, every team is different. We just didn’t play well. That’s one week. That’s not Browns being Browns, that’s Browns being poorly on one week. “So, again, everybody’s afforded their opinion. And the only way to change people’s opinion is to play better. That’s a fact. We don’t want to be considered an also-ran, then we have to play better. We have to coach better, and we have to play better.” At this point, Monken is right — the only way the Browns can change their perception is by winning. We’ll see if they can at least be competitive against the Buccaneers on Sunday, though that will be unlikely if Deshaun Watson does not play any better at quarterback.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Senate advances the Protect College Sports Act
summary: ESPN has gotten its apparent wish.
full_text: ESPN has gotten its apparent wish. Partially, for now. The Senate has passed the Protect College Sports Act, by a vote of 74-24. It's a procedural move and not yet a full vote of the Senate. The vote comes three days after ESPN put Senator Ted Cruz (R-Texas), one of the bill's sponsors, on its flagship college football show to advocate for the passage of the act, without a contemporaneous opposing point of view. And while Stephen A. Smith has apparently chastised me for suggesting that everyone at ESPN supports the Protect College Sports Act, I don't believe that. It was not my intent to put everyone at ESPN in the same bucket, and I apologize if I created that impression. My point was and is that ESPN's corporate position seems to be that it supports the bill, as evidenced by the fact that two of its most prominent college football analysts (Nick Saban and Pat McAfee) have argued for its passage on GameDay without any real pushback by other panelists, by Disney's reported lobbying for the bill, and by the misguided decision to platform Cruz without offering a voice representing the other side. Here's a thought — they could have let Smith interview Cruz. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) also opposes the Protect College Sports Act. I'll be interviewing him on Thursday morning, for a special edition of #PFTPM. I'd love to chop it up with Stephen A., too. We agree on plenty of things. On the things we disagree, there's a chance that, through open and honest discourse, we'd better understand each other's points of view. The country currently needs a lot more of that. The country does not need a federal law that "saves" college sports, in my opinion. College sports are doing just fine, and the system should be required to clean up its own mess without a federal bailout that artificially limits the compensation and freedom of the people who generate the vast majority of the revenue, while leaving unrestricted the ability of coaches to hopscotch the map in chase of their next bag of cash.
author: Mike Florio

title: Patriots, Mack Hollins agreed to make his 2026 incentives harder to earn
summary: It's going to be a little harder for Patriots receiver Mack Hollins to boost his shoe budget.
full_text: '' It's going to be a little harder for Patriots receiver Mack Hollins to boost his shoe budget. The fact that he doesn’t seem to ever wear them makes that less of a problem. Via Spotrac, the Patriots and Hollins agreed to a 2026 revision that converts some of the potential payments into not-likely-to-be-earned incentives. The move shifts money from the 2026 salary cap to 2027, if the incentives are reached. Previously, Hollins was due to get $300,000 for catching 30 passes, another $300,000 for catching 40, and another $400,000 for catching 50. The new version moves the magic numbers to 47, 50, and 55, respectively. Last year, Hollins caught 46 passes. Which unlocked $600,000 in extra pay. And which made $600,000 of the incentive package "likely to be earned" in 2026, with those dollars counting against the 2026 cap. The new deal was finalized on September 1. Given that Hollins apparently got nothing in return for the adjustment, the leverage to get him to agree would have been a not-so-subtle suggestion that he'd be released before Week 1, when his $2.9 million base salary would have become guaranteed as termination pay. (He also has $750,000 in per-game active roster bonuses.) It's odd to think the Patriots were considering cutting Hollins. Albert Breer of SI.com recently reported that at least one contending team expressed interest in trading for Hollins, and the Patriots declined . Hollins could have forced the issue, become a free agent, and signed with that team (or any other). The likely problem was the timing. Hollins would have been scrambling for a job, at a time when rosters were set. The team that had been interested in trading for him may have addressed its needs elsewhere. And, even if someone would have given Hollins the same terms he had with the Patriots, Hollins would have had to embrace a new city, new team, new coaching staff, new everything only days away from Week 1. The good news for Hollins is that the A.J. Brown injury will give Hollins more opportunities to get toward 47, 50, and/or 55 receptions. In Week 1, Hollins had four catches. That projects to 68 for the season, which would get him the full $1 million — and which would make all of it count against the 2027 cap.

title: Jaguars place B.J. Green on IR, sign Jack Kiser to 53-man roster
summary: The Jaguars have made a few moves on Wednesday morning.
full_text: The Jaguars have made a few moves on Wednesday morning. Jacksonville announced the club has placed defensive end B.J. Green on injured reserve, signed linebacker Jack Kiser to the 53-man roster, and signe defensive end BJ Ojulari to the practice squad. Green is dealing with an elbow injury. title: Keenan Allen formally charged with two misdemeanors from August arrest
summary: Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen has been formally charged with a pair of misdemeanors related to his August arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence.
full_text: Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen has been formally charged with a pair of misdemeanors related to his August arrest on suspicion of driving under the influence. According to multiple reports, Allen has been formally charged with with operating a vehicle with an alcohol concentration equivalent (ACE) of 0.15 or more and operating a vehicle while intoxicated. The former charge is a Class A misdemeanor which carries a possible jail sentence of up to one year and a fine of no more than $5000. The other charge can result in a jail term of no more than 60 days and a fine of no more than $500. Colts General Manager Chris Ballard said that any team discipline would be handled internally. Allen also faces possible league discipline, which is typically a three-game suspension for alcohol-related offenses. Nathan Brown of the Indianapolis Star notes that the collective bargaining agreement allows for enhanced penalties given Allen's ACE level. Allen played in last Sunday's loss to the Ravens and had six catches for 32 yards.
author: Josh Alper

title: Could Carson Wentz play his way into the Vikings' QB1 job?
summary: Wentz performed well in Week 1. If it continues, the Vikings could stick with the hot hand.
full_text: Most casual observers of the NFL were surprised to see quarterback Carson Wentz enter Sunday's game for the Vikings after Kyler Murray suffered a concussion on the third drive of the game. There's another potential surprise in the pipeline. If Wentz keeps playing well and winning, he could end up hanging onto the job even after Murray is cleared to return. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network floated that idea on Tuesday night. And it would be a stunner; Wentz was never in the competition to start, if the competition between Murray and J.J. McCarthy was even a real competition. (It likely wasn't.) Last year, when Wentz was playing in place of McCarthy, who suffered an ankle sprain in Week 2, there was a sense that Wentz could keep the job even after McCarthy was ready to play. The key factor in that was simple — Wentz and receiver Justin Jefferson had a more effective in-game connection than McCarthy and Jefferson. A season-ending injury to Wentz's left shoulder, through which he played for multiple weeks, ended that debate. This year, a fresh debate could emerge — if Murray can't return for Sunday's game against the Bears and if Wentz can engineer an upset at Soldier Field. Rapoport calls the possibility an "excellent problem." Still, the best problem is no problem at all. It won't be easy to manage Murray if he believes he lost his job over a concussion suffered on the third drive of the opening game of the season. In the end, however, it's all about winning games. If Wentz keeps winning, maybe he'll keep playing. Either way, the Vikings have a pair of top-two draft picks who grew up rooting for the team. Murray, for now, isn't healthy enough to play. Wentz is. He'll get an opportunity to extend his run if he can continue to run the offense in a way that helps Minnesota score more points than the other team. Which, in a numbers-driven league, continues to be the only statistic that matters.

title: Ranking 5 NFL teams that need a win the most in Week 2, including the Cowboys and Patriots
summary: It's already a make-or-break week for some of these NFL teams
full_text:
The "must-win" label is often overplayed in sports, especially when it's handed out early in a given season. That said, a handful of teams dropped their season openers and now have their backs somewhat against the wall as they look toward Week 2.
While falling to 0-2 isn't exactly the same nail in the coffin as it was before playoff expansion, it creates an uphill battle nonetheless. At the very least, doubt starts to creep in at 0-2 about whether or not all that preseason optimism was based in reality.
Below, we'll highlight five teams still hunting their first win of 2026 and rank them by who needs to notch a win most.
NFL odds via DraftKings Sportsbook.
Week 2 opponent : vs. New York Giants (Monday) Week 2 odds : Rams -7 (-115), Rams ML (-355)
Los Angeles is still the odds-on favorite to win Super Bowl LXI, but some air has been let out of the balloon since the regular season kicked off. Sean McVay's plan of arriving a day before their international matchup with the 49ers in Australia blew up in his face as the Rams fell flat in a 27-7 defeat. On top of making the 15-hour flight home at 0-1, L.A. also lost its offseason prize in the process, as pass rusher Myles Garrett was placed on injured reserve due to a knee injury that requires surgery.
They'll look to rebound now that they are back stateside, where they'll host the New York Giants on "Monday Night Football" to conclude Week 2. The Giants are coming off an upset win against the Cowboys in the opener, but the Rams are a sizable home favorite, currently laying a full touchdown. If they lose this matchup and the offense continues to look stagnant like it did in Melbourne, the panic level will almost certainly reach a fever pitch. After all, the Rams are back on the road after this game, visiting the Denver Broncos in Week 3 and then the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4. Those are two of the toughest road environments in the NFL , and with the added pressure of possibly still searching for their first win in both of those contests, things could get really tight in that Rams locker room.
Even after that road trip, they face the Buffalo Bills in Week 5 when they return to SoFi Stadium, so there is no letup in the early portion of this schedule. This is a game the oddsmakers believe L.A. should win with relative ease, and they'll need to pile these types of victories up where they can.
Week 2 opponent : vs. Jacksonville Jaguars Week 2 odds : Broncos -2.5 (-118), Broncos ML (-148)
Denver entered the season with the reputation of having one of the top defenses in the NFL. At least for one night, however, that notion was dispelled when the Kansas City Chiefs demolished them 31-10 on Monday night.
According to Next Gen Stats , the Broncos' defense missed 28 tackles against Kansas City and allowed 247 yards after those missed tackles. Eight different defenders missed multiple tackles. Yuck. On top of the defensive issues, the Broncos' offense was clunky with Davis Webb now calling plays instead of Sean Payton.
After dropping the opener against a division rival, Denver cannot afford to not only go 0-2 on the season but also lose another key head-to-head tiebreaker against a team they could be jockeying for playoff position against in Jacksonville. Last year, the Jaguars went into Mile High and handed the Broncos a 34-20 defeat in Week 16, so they've proven to be quite comfortable in this spot.
The Broncos are accustomed to slow starts under Payton, as this would be the third 0-2 start in four seasons under his helm. That said, if the defense looks like it did in Week 1 and the offensive play calling doesn't improve as they go 0-2 this time around, things could look a little more dire than those previous seasons, particularly with a daunting slate of games (vs. Rams, at 49ers, at Chargers , and vs. Seahawks ) on the horizon.
Week 2 opponent : at New York Jets Week 2 odds : Packers -4.5 (+100), Packers ML (-205)
Green Bay utterly collapsed against the Vikings on Sunday, blowing a 12-point second-half lead to Carson Wentz , who entered the game for the injured Kyler Murray . This is now the sixth straight loss for the Packers dating back to last season (including the playoffs), and the underlying metrics from Jordan Love's day on Sunday were not encouraging. Love's off-target rate (23.8%) was the highest among quarterbacks in Week 1 and, on top of his interception, he had two others dropped by Minnesota.
Despite all that, they are road favorites as they head to MetLife Stadium to face the Jets. While New York did look vastly improved from what they were a year ago, thanks to their offseason additions, they are still the Jets. If Green Bay fancies itself as a playoff-caliber team in the NFC, it should be able to head into this road environment and pull out a win against a team that is widely expected to be on the outside looking in on the postseason this year.
Meanwhile, they were the lone team in the NFC North to come out winless in Week 1 and already have a division loss on the résumé, too. While the Jets are an AFC opponent, they need to pick up the layup wins when they are in front of them.
Week 2 opponent : vs. Pittsburgh Steelers Week 2 odds : Patriots -5.5 (-105), Patriots ML (-218)
The Patriots -- specifically Drake Maye -- fell on their face in a Week 1 loss to the Seahawks. Coming into the season, New England was pegged as a regression candidate after making the Super Bowl last year, thanks, in part, to a cakewalk of a schedule. While they were underdogs entering the season opener, it did appear like the seas were parting for them yet again, with Sam Darnold going down with an injury early in the first quarter. That suddenly turned this into a very winnable game for New England, who would now only need to out-duel backup Drew Lock . Well, Maye tossed three interceptions in the fourth quarter, including a game-clinching pick in the end zone.
Mike Vrabel's team will now try to pick up the pieces in what should be another winnable game at home against Pittsburgh. The Steelers' offense struggled against a battered Falcons defense in Week 1, so if New England can't create distance between them on Sunday afternoon, real concerns are starting about what this team truly is. They could also be looking at the possibility of a 0-4 start if they lose here. After Week 2, the Patriots will be on the road for two weeks (at Jacksonville and at Buffalo). They most likely won't be favored in either of those contests, making this as close to a kitchen-sink game as it can be for this time of the year.
Week 2 opponent : vs. Washington Commanders Week 2 odds : Cowboys -4.5 (-105), Cowboys ML (-225)
After all the talk about Dallas' new-and-improved defense coming into 2026, the unit didn't look impressive at all in a Week 1 loss to the New York Giants. Despite a slew of new faces, it was largely the same story for the Cowboys' defense, allowing New York to convert 9 of 11 third-down opportunities and score touchdowns on all four of their red zone trips. They were also bullied on the ground, allowing 165 yards and a touchdown on 4.5 yards per carry.
For his part, Dak Prescott also made some questionable decisions with the football, including an inexplicable interception before the half that helped New York go up by a touchdown.
If the defense doesn't show signs of life and/or Prescott turns the ball over at a critical juncture again as they head home to face the Commanders, the Cowboys will be a Defcon 1. That would not only mean they've fallen to 0-2 for the season, but also that they've dropped two divisional games in the process, which could prove monumental for tiebreakers later this season. When you consider an international matchup with the Baltimore Ravens in Week 3 and then a road matchup against the Texans in Week 4, things could start slipping quickly for Jerry Jones' club, so a win here would do a lot to calm the nerves around AT&T Stadium.

title: How Tom Brady made Joe Thomas cry and why Browns legend turned down chance to play with Peyton Manning
summary: The Hall of Fame left tackle relished his football home in Cleveland, but he eventually realized his impact couldn't save the Browns
full_text:
Many NFL players' careers have gone to die on the Cleveland Browns , but no one's prime was wasted as a Brown in the 21st century quite like Pro Football Hall of Fame left tackle Joe Thomas'.
After being selected third overall in the 2007 NFL Draft , Thomas lived up to the Browns' faith in him: he earned 10 Pro Bowl selections, six first-team All-Pro selections, two second-team All-Pro selections and a 2010 All-Decade team selection. The rest of Cleveland's roster didn't live up to his standards, going 48-112 in his first 10 seasons. That was the second-worst record in the entire league in that span ahead of only the Rams at 46-113-1. Thomas would convince himself year after year that the Browns had what it took despite reality painting a different picture.
"The way I entered every season was like, 'if I need to get the most out of myself, I've got to convince myself this is a Super Bowl roster. That's the mentality I have to have when I'm training, when I'm practicing, when I'm going through film study,'" Thomas said on the "Bussin' With The Boys" podcast. "And so you trick yourself every year, but after a while, you're not that dumb anymore."
Entering his 10th season of trying to gaslight himself into thinking the new season would be different, Thomas began to see the writing on the wall with players being traded away for draft picks. He still tried to trick himself in 2016, but the evidence in front of him became too great to ignore. Getting blown out 33-13 at home against Tom Brady and the New England Patriots in Week 5 of the 2016 season demoralized Thomas, removing any illusion Cleveland was going to be relevant that year after the defeat dropped the Browns to 0-5. Brady shredded the Browns' defense to the tune of 406 yards passing on 28 of 40 passing for a 127.7 passer rating that day.
"Then, about midway through that 10th season, we were playing the Patriots. Tom Brady comes to town, and I f---ing hated Tom Brady, as everybody did in the league. I hated the Patriots. I just wanted to smash him so bad," Thomas said. "We lost like 30 to 0. And I remember sitting in the car after the game, and I was just crying. I had ice on both elbows and knees. I was in pain. My wife was driving, and I was just looking out the window. It was that moment when I realized I'd been kind of fooling myself for a while, and we were not going to win no matter what I did."
His wife asking him if he didn't perform well cut him to his core because Thomas was on his way to his 10th consecutive Pro Bowl season in 2016, but it didn't matter at all. That's why he sought help from a mental professional, meeting with the team psychologist.
She finally said, 'Are you okay? Did you have a bad game?' Then the tears really came because I said 'I played a perfect game, and we lost by 30,'" Thomas said. "It really sunk in at that moment that you don't control the situation anymore. That feeling of loss of control is really hard. No matter what situation you're in in life, it just feels like everything I'm working for, I have no control over the outcome. That's a bad feeling. I ended up meeting with the team psychologist and talking to somebody about it because it had been almost 10 years built up to that moment when you come to the realization that I'm kind of fooling myself. 'We're not that team and we really don't have a chance. And I don't impact this game the way I'd hoped.'"
Thomas could have avoided that painful realization in 2016 if he had just taken up Pro Football Hall of Fame quarterback Peyton Manning's offer to come be his left tackle on the Denver Broncos a year earlier in 2015. That year, Broncos All-Pro left tackle Ryan Clady tore his ACL. That's when Thomas got a call from an unknown number with a Denver area code.
"It's Peyton. 'Hey buddy, this is your drinking buddy from the Pro Bowl.' You know his voice immediately. ... He said 'well, hey listen. We lost our left tackle. I really want you to block for me, but the Browns are worried you're kind of their franchise," Manning told Thomas. "'They love you over there. We got a fair deal on the table, but [John] Elway is telling me it's not going to get done unless you go up in your GM's office and tell them you want to be traded.'"
Thomas turned Manning's offer down because of his undying love for the team that drafted him third overall years ago.
"Well, that's a pretty difficult thing to turn down, but I said 'I am happy here in Cleveland. If the deal gets done on its own merit, great. If not, I'm not willing to try and force a trade,'" Thomas replied.
Then, Manning got desperate, so he tried to goad Thomas into getting comfortable being traded with humor. That didn't work either.
"'Alright, how about this? Go up into [general manger] Ray Farmer's office, when he's not there of course, pull your pants down and take a shit on his desk. That way, you don't have to say anything about it, but he has to trade you at that point,'" Manning told Thomas. "I got a good laugh out of that one, and I said 'I'll consider it Peyton, I appreciate that.'"
That loyalty ended up being a one-way street in terms of an investment to winning between Thomas and the Browns, and he unknowingly turned down a Super Bowl 50 championship ring by doing so. Manning went out on top, even though he was a shell of his five-time NFL MVP self, because he had prime Von Miller and one of the best defenses in football giving him the help he needed. Instead, all Thomas can do now is shake his head and laugh at the insanity of his 11-year case of Stockholm syndrome in Cleveland.

title: Can Derrick Henry break NFL rushing record? All-time leader Emmitt Smith thinks so
summary: Henry sits at No. 10 on the all-time rushing list and still has some work to do to break Smith's record
full_text:
Emmitt Smith has held one of sports' most prestigious records since 2002, when he broke Walter Payton's 16,726-yard rushing record, set in 1984. Smith stretched the record to 18,355 yards before retiring after the 2004 season.
No one has seriously come close to matching Smith. Frank Gore, who broke into the NFL a year after Smith retired, came closest this century with 16,000 rushing yards. The only current back that has a legitimate chance to eventually catch Smith is Ravens running back Derrick Henry , who is currently 10th all time with 13,162 yards.
While Henry still has a ways to go, Smith feels that Henry could make a strong chase at his record and could possibly surpass him as the NFL's career rushing king.
"Oh yeah, I think it's possible," Smith recently said . "Derrick Henry is a bigger back. He takes good care of his body. He's in great shape. Y'all don't know this, but Derrick Henry broke my high school record. He broke my state high school record. So I believe he can do it again."
While Henry has the best chance of any current running back to eventually break Smith's record, it's anything but a sure thing.
Henry is currently 5,193 yards from matching Smith's record. For him to pass Smith, Henry either needs three seasons of at least 1,731 rushing yards or four years of roughly 1,300 yards.
Since 2018, Henry has averaged 1,473 rushing yards per season. That stretch included a 2,000-yard season (in 2020) and the greatest season for a running back in NFL history over the age of 30 in 2024, when he ran for 1,921 yards. Last season, Henry ran for an impressive 1,595 yards, the third-most-prolific season for an age-31 running back in league history, behind only Curtis Martin (2004) and Tiki Barber (2006).
Henry showed no signs of slowing down in Week 1. In addition to rushing for 144 yards, Henry scored three touchdowns while moving into third all time in career touchdown runs .
THE KING!!!! 32-YARD TOUCHDOWN FROM @KingHenry_2 FOR HIS SECOND TD OF THE DAY!!! Tune in on @NFLonCBS and @ParamountPlus . pic.twitter.com/TDSbqCwka3
Despite being 32 (the age when most running backs are either already retired or in steep decline), Henry continues to play at an extremely high level. That will have to continue for him to have a chance to break Smith's record.
While extremely rare, a running back continuing to pile up big numbers in his mid-30s has happened before. John Riggins, whose number the Commanders will retire this season, ran for 1,347 yards in his age-34 season and 1,239 yards in his age-35 season. It should be noted that Riggins took a year off during his prime and starred during a nine-game, strike-shortened season, so his success late in his career was at least partly a byproduct of less wear and tear earlier in his career.
Henry has displayed incredible longevity and, as Smith alluded, takes exceptionally good care of himself, which is undoubtedly a reason for his sustained success. That said, Henry will need a truly historic run to catch Smith. At this point, given how many yards Henry still needs, the odds of him eventually passing Smith are slim, though not certainly impossible.
Smith aside, Henry has a chance to pass several other NFL icons in the record books this season.
On the all-time rushing list, Henry is 98 yards from passing Eric Dickerson, 501 yards from passing Jerome Bettis, 523 yards from passing LaDainian Tomlinson, and 940 yards from passing Curtis Martin, who is currently sixth. Barring injury, Henry should pass each of these Hall of Fame running backs in 2026.
Next season, Henry should be in position to pass Adrian Peterson (14,918 yards) and Barry Sanders (15,269 yards). If he does that, Henry would enter the 2028 season trailing only Smith, Payton and Gore on the all-time list.
In career touchdown runs, Henry trails only Smith (164 touchdowns) and Tomlinson (145). It's possible that Henry passes Tomlinson this season and will only have Smith ahead of him entering the 2027 season.
Henry's future spot in the Pro Football Hall of Fame is already secure and has been for some time. Of the eligible running backs with 12,000 career rushing yards, every one of them is in the Hall of Fame. Henry will join them in Canton, Ohio, as soon as he is eligible. Everything he does now is icing on the cake.

title: NFL Week 2 odds, picks: Jets continue to stay frisky, while Baker Mayfield torches former Browns team
summary: Tyler Sullivan picks every game on the Week 2 schedule, plus five locks against the spread
full_text:
We are off and running in the 2026 regular season and are coming off an opening weekend where we escaped Week 1 with a stellar record on the whole. For the slate, I went 13-3 on straight-up picks and 9-7 ATS. That was good for the best among CBS Sports experts straight up and tied for second against the spread.
The only unfortunate aspect of my weekend was that some of the locks within my five Locks of the Week were faulty. I was 2-3 ATS on my five best bets, with the Jets ' upset win in Nashville and Jacksonville's throttling of the Browns as the lone covers. The Houston Texans nearly swung the day for us as they had the Buffalo Bills on the ropes, but Josh Allen was simply too much to slay, so we'll look to keep the overall momentum rolling in Week 2 while cleaning things up with my locks.
As we turn our attention to the upcoming slate, we're somewhat going back to the well with a couple of teams, attacking the Browns and buying the Jets with the points.
It seems like Cooper Rush is going to get another start for Atlanta, so we'll gladly fade him after a rough debut with the Falcons in Week 1. Out of every starting quarterback that took the field in Week 1, no one has a worse passer rating than Rush (54.9). There was essentially no vertical passing game as Rush averaged just 3.5 air yards per attempt (31st among QBs). Despite that, he still had an off-target rate of 13.6% (22nd). So, while the Panthers ' defense was pantsed by the Bears in Week 1 to the tune of 59 points allowed, they won't face nearly the firepower under center as they did when squaring up against Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams . Meanwhile, lost in the Bears lighting it up, Bryce Young put together a strong effort, with his .29 EPA per dropback ranking sixth-highest among all quarterbacks in Week 1. The Panthers QB also owns a 4-1 SU and ATS record when he starts against Atlanta.
Projected score: Panthers 24, Falcons 20 The pick: Panthers -1
Listen, this might be the last time in our lives that we'll be able to bet against Deshaun Watson , so we HAVE to take this opportunity while it's still there. The Browns QB looked about as you'd expect him to look in the opening loss to Jacksonville. He didn't seem comfortable in the pocket at all, tossed an interception on his opening possession, and nearly had two more turnovers. Dating to before his Achilles injuries, Watson is 0-6 SU and 1-5 ATS over his last six starts. Meanwhile, the Browns are 1-10 ATS in their last 11 road games when they are a dog of 6-plus points.
While Watson won't provide much resistance for the Bucs defense, old friend Baker Mayfield is likely chomping at the bit to square off against his former team. This will be just the second game against Cleveland since he was traded in the summer of 2022. Mayfield lost his first matchup against the Browns while a member of the Panthers, but has since revitalized his career in Tampa and will likely be looking to run it up with his college of skill-position players. The Bucs are 3-0 SU in home openers with Mayfield.
Projected score: Buccaneers 30, Browns 13 The pick: Buccaneers -8.5
It's hard to call a Week 2 matchup a kitchen-sink game or any team, but I sort of feel that way with the Patriots. They completely collapsed in the fourth quarter and lost a winnable game against the Seahawks in the season opener. After this game on Sunday, they'll begin a two-week road trip where they'll head to Jacksonville and Buffalo. The Patriots shouldn't expect to be favored in either of those matchups, so if they drop this home opener to Pittsburgh, they're looking down the barrel of a potential 0-4 start.
While they did lose A.J. Brown (ankle) to injury, I think New England should be able to outpace the Steelers ' offense. Aaron Rodgers was tied for the fourth-worst EPA per dropback in the NFL in Week 1 as the Pittsburgh offense averaged just 4.1 yards per play against Atlanta. The Patriots boast a far better defense than the Falcons, with All-Pro corner Christian Gonzalez and a pass rush that was surprisingly disruptive in Week 1.
Remember, the Steelers went into Foxborough in Week 3 last year and pulled out a 21-14 win. In that loss, the Patriots turned the ball over five (!) times. Mike Vrabel will almost certainly remind them of that game and push them to right the wrong here.
Drake Maye is also 6-0 SU and 5-1 ATS as a 3-plus point favorite at home in his career.
Projected score: Patriots 24, Steelers 17 The pick: Patriots -5.5
Can you believe it? We're backing the Jets in back-to-back weeks! Did we slip into the Twilight Zone or something? Unlike last week, however, we're not taking them to pull off the outright win (although I was tempted). Instead, we're looking for them to merely cover as they host the Packers in the home opener. While it was against Tennessee, New York looked far improved from last year's squad. Specifically, they got stable quarterback play from Geno Smith , who was the only quarterback in the entire Week 1 slate to not have an off-target throw. Meanwhile, the defense showed signs of life, specifically with No. 2 overall pick David Bailey tallying a sack in his debut.
As we look at Green Bay, I just don't have a lot of faith in the Packers right now as a road favorite. They collapsed against the Vikings , and Jordan Love did not look good in the process. In stark contrast to Smith, Love's off-target rate was the highest among every quarterback in Week 1 (23.8%). On top of throwing an interception against Minnesota, the Vikings dropped two others, so it was nearly an even more disastrous day for the Packers' quarterback.
They may win because they have a smidge more talent, but it'll be within the number.
Projected score: Packers 24, Jets 21 The pick: Jets +3.5
Maybe it's a trap, but I don't care. I'll fade Cam Ward and the Titans until they give me a reason not to. Ward ranked 26th in the league in Week 1 in EPA per dropback as well as off-target rate in a loss to New York at home. He was sacked three times in the opener, and will now face an Eagles front that will continue to apply pressure. Tennessee scored just 10 points in Week 1, which was the fewest point total in a season opener at home in franchise history. It's hard to imagine this unit suddenly finding success against a superior defense that took it to them on Sunday.
Meanwhile, Breece Hall averaged 4.6 yards per carry while piling up 102 yards and a touchdown on the ground against Robert Saleh's defense in Week 1, and I expect Saquon Barkley to carry the baton with a similar showing in Week 2. This should be a double-digit win by Philadelphia.
Projected score: Eagles 27, Titans 17 The pick: Eagles -7

title: Cowboys' Caleb Downs explains why historically bad Week 1 defense is 'very fixable'
summary: Dallas produced one of the NFL's worst defensive performances since the start of 2025, but its first-round rookie says the mistakes are correctable
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys entered the 2026 season full of hope for a new era of defense. After firing defensive coordinator Matt Eberflus , Dallas hired 34-year-old, longtime Vic Fangio staffer Christian Parker, and also revamped its roster. Nearly half, 46.2%, per the Dallas Morning News , of the snaps taken on Dallas' defense in 2025 are no longer on the team.
However, the on-field performance was more of the same in a 28-20 road loss to the New York Giants . New York converted 82% of its third downs, with one of those stops being the game-ending knee down. That figure was New York's best third-down conversion rate in a single game since 1978.
Based on defensive expected points added (EPA)/ per drive in TruMedia, the Cowboys delivered the worst effort by any team in Week 1, and it was worse than all of their defensive games last year. Of the 576 defensive performances since the start of the 2025 season, it ranked 574th. Their seven defensive possessions yielded four touchdowns, one takeaway via fumble recovery, a punt and the game ending.
So how did the Cowboys' latest stinker happen after all that change?
"To lose contain on a guy like Jaxson (Dart) that is that athletic, and it was multiple guys at multiple times. ... We have Jayden [Daniels and the Washington Commanders ] this week, and then you guys have maybe heard of Lamar Jackson [and the Baltimore Ravens ] coming in a couple weeks. So we certainly have to get better with our discipline," coach Brian Schottenheimer said. "The other thing that I will say, looking at the game, that we need to be better in is our communication on defense. ... Communication is two parts. It's the person that gives [the call], and the person that receives it has to acknowledge it. Some of the things that we did in the red zone late where we didn't have anybody accounting for [running back Devin] Singletary, who is a pretty dynamic player. Those were communication issues. That can't happen because those are self-inflicted wounds that get you beat."
In an otherwise forgettable night, the debut of 11th overall pick Caleb Downs was a positive one. The ex-Ohio State safety racked up seven total tackles, one sack and one forced fumble. Dart targeted Downs once and completed a pass for five yards on the rookie's 29 coverage snaps, per TruMedia. In college, Downs was relied on to help with on-field communication, and he didn't put the blame on Parker, a first-time defensive coordinator, not getting the call in fast enough.
"I think it's just first-game execution honestly," Downs told CBS Sports related to Week 1 communication. "I don't necessarily think it's not getting a call or anything like that. I think it's just making sure we're detailed in our work and doing our jobs at the highest level more so than anything else. Just executing our job is the biggest thing."
While Schottenheimer had plenty to gripe about with his defense after Week 1, Downs wasn't one of them. He's already in love with his ability to harass the quarterback, something he did with a strip sack of Dart with 2:36 left in the first half. Unfortunately for the Cowboys, New York jumped on the football as it did on three of the four fumbles Dallas forced.
"I think Caleb played really, really well," Schottenheimer said. "Jaxson Dart never saw him on the blitz. He gets a free run and the ball goes spiraling through the air, and the 320-pound guard [Jon Runyan Jr.] catches it and rumbles for five yards. That's kind of how the night went for us. I think that's one of the positives of what we did on defense: we attacked the ball. We had four forced fumbles. ... Caleb is a guy that can move around, but we like him down near the line of scrimmage."
Caleb Downs with a HUGE hit on Jaxson Dart 😤 DALvsNYG on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/6x4h1EbLxb
Early in the game, Downs functioned as a safety in Dallas' base defense and then closer to the line as a nickel corner/hybrid linebacker near the line of scrimmage in sub-packages. That's how former NFL coach Matt Patricia, now Ohio State's defensive coordinator, used him as a chess piece up and down the field.
"Yeah, a lot similar to college, being able to move around," Downs said. "So being able to play, whether it's nickel, being able to play safety and then third down, being able to play dime as well. I think just being able to make plays wherever you're at, that's the biggest thing. So I have confidence in my ability, and that's what I'm going to go out and do."
Dallas' plan at deep safety with Malik Hooker sidelined for what they hope is only a couple of weeks with a forearm fracture is to have seven-year veteran P.J. Locke fill in at that spot so that Downs can be freed up to play more of his hybrid role along the line of scrimmage.
"I think I can play the run game really well. Play the pass game, whatever it is, whether it's man or dropping zones," Downs said. "I'm an extra corner or extra linebacker. Whatever you need."
The Cowboys trust Downs to handle whatever they throw at him because of the way he attacks watching film and preparing himself to play each and every week.
"Man, [I] probably sound like a broken record. The way he prepares, the way he practices is not like, I don't want to say any. It's not like most rookies I've been around. It's different. There's a different mindset," Schottenheimer said entering Week 1. "There's a different competitive fire in this kid. He craves coaching. He cannot get coached enough. And I think at the end of the day, that's why he's such a good player. I think you look at him and just the way he's always played the game, he plays it with instincts. ... He works his butt off at studying the X and the O's part of it. So unique young man, very special talent."
Downs and Parker are the two new faces of the Cowboys' defense, along with four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Quinnen Williams . They walked off the bus together at MetLife Stadium Sunday night, and Downs sees symmetry in their career trajectories.
"We're going through the same journey at the same time," Downs said. "It's my first season, and it's his first season calling the plays and being the defensive coordinator. So I think there's a lot of similarities there, and we're just trying to succeed at what we do, and that's the biggest thing."
After their deflating primetime defeat, Parker pulled Downs aside immediately after landing back home to talk about what needs to change entering Week 2 against the Washington Commanders.
"When we got off the plane for a couple minutes, just talking about some of the things we needed to correct for this coming week and really just basic defense," Downs said. "How we need to adjust and do certain things. Just talking about this coming week and how we're going to prepare a little bit differently."
Downs' tone when describing that chat oozed with confidence. Why? Because there is a belief that the issue that plagued them in Week 1 can be course-corrected shortly.
"Everything that we made mistakes on is very fixable," Downs said. "Defense is pretty simple. At the end of the day, it's not like we're playing rocket science. It's just we got to do our jobs when we're on the field, and that's the biggest thing."
Schottenheimer had a similarly productive chat both after the game and on Monday back home at The Star, Dallas' team facility. He came away from that conversation feeling convinced he made the right choice to hire Parker.
"He and I were on the same page with that, which is a good thing," Schottenheimer said. "And then this morning he was amazing with the staff and having hard conversations and real conversations. "And this is not just the players, this is us as a staff. That's a leader. That's a leader of men. ... I'm around him every day. ... I have no question Christian Parker is the right guy for this job. He's an outstanding coach. He will learn from this, just like our young players are going to learn from this. We're going to play our young players this…
author: Garrett Podell
