title: Ranking the five best 2026 NFL Draft classes after Week 1: Chiefs rookies shine brightest
summary: These five teams' rookies produced the most during Week 1 of the NFL season
full_text:
They say you can't evaluate a draft class until after three seasons. Unfortunately, it's 2026, and no one has that much patience anymore, so how about we do it after one week? As always, the caveat is: this is one game. This is not the end-all, be-all. But with most things, it's better to look good early on than bad.
These are the top-five draft classes after the first week of the season.
Highlight: Peter Woods rare athleticism Lowlight: Mansoor Delane's shoulder injury
There were whispers about Brett Veach having another masterclass draft last April, and they've now turned into roars. Peter Woods was already making special plays as a pass-rusher and in the run game. He also chased down a running back from behind on a flat route. His addition will allow Steve Spagnuolo to be more measured with how many snaps they give to 32-year-old Chris Jones going forward.
Peter Woods with one of the most athletic recoveries vs. a double team you'll ever see from a DT pic.twitter.com/CdMDIiJ7CB
Top-10 corner Mansoor Delane unfortunately left the game after three snaps with a shoulder injury, but the injury occurred on a play where he ran a dig route for Courtland Sutton and picked off a pass.
Mansoor Delane Every Snap in NFL Debut vs Broncos pic.twitter.com/0rrFJYFzhS
Then there was second-round edge rusher R Mason Thomas , who had a crucial sack in a two-minute drill before the half, where he teleported underneath Mike McGlinchey with a spin move.
Rookie R Mason Thomas with the spin move right into a sack 💪 DENvsKC on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/mVVJ07s2NB
Oh, and then Day 3 running back Emmett Johnson made as many people miss on two catches Monday night (six) as Isiah Pacheco and Kareem Hunt on 37 combined catches last season. It's hard to swing and hit harder than the Chiefs did with their first three picks, at least in Monday night's win.
Highlight: Austin Barber locking down right guard Lowlight: KC Concepcion's ball security
Lost in the ugliness of the Browns quarterback position was the fact that the Browns look like they've clocked yet another impressive draft haul. The Browns have four starters on offense from the 2026 draft class in Spencer Fano , Austin Barber, KC Concepcion, and Denzel Boston , with Emmanuel McNeil-Warren filling in for 14 snaps defensively. While they weren't as obviously slam dunks as the Chiefs, there were big-time flashes for all of the offensive starters.
Concepcion, in particular, already looks like the Browns' best playmaker. His ability to separate was on full display.
KC Concepcion consistently shows strength & fluidity when running routes. Being able to stem inside, get vertical to the proper depth, and roll into this deep sail route all while a defender on the hip isn’t easy. pic.twitter.com/rdEsYTGOJi
While he didn't have any drops that he was known for in college, Concepcion did have an ugly fumble, which was also a problem for him in school, with four fumbles on 185 career receptions.
The most surprising standout was third-rounder Barber. A career tackle at Florida, Barber kicked inside and flipped to the right side for the Browns. He was incredibly clean for a rookie in his first career start. PFF had him as the highest-graded rookie offensive lineman of the week. While there were more concerns on tape than that grade may suggest, Barber looked like he'll be a long-term starter at the position for Cleveland.
Highlight: Vega Ioane's run game dominance Lowlight: Zion Young's 12 forgettable snaps
The Ravens are the only team on this list that didn't have multiple first-rounders. That didn't stop them from getting a big impact from their rookie class, however. The big reason why is first-rounder Vega Ioane. He was the single best rookie I saw on tape in Week 1. He was dominant in the run game at right guard against the Colts , and while there was a trio of reps he'd want back in pass protection, there were others where he paved the way for Lamar Jackson's scrambles. Considering the state of the Ravens' right guard position a year ago, this draft pick could not have had better early returns.
Vega Ioane was the closest thing I saw to a Pro-Bowler in the rookie class Week 1. A few reps he'd want back in pass pro, but sheer dominance otherwise pic.twitter.com/2cau8PLgNY
The Ravens also got meaningful contributions from third-round receiver Ja'Kobi Lane and fourth-round tight end Matthew Hibner , who played 27 and 23 snaps, respectively. Hibner looked like a very capable TE2, while Lane looked like he'll be a red zone favorite for Lamar Jackson. Lane saw three targets inside the opposing 20-yard line, with one touchdown called back by a penalty.
Highlight: Most rookie starters in the NFL Lowlight: Most rookie starters shouldn't have been starting
No team in the NFL hit reset harder this season than the Miami Dolphins . All told, they had 368 of a possible 1,353 snaps Sunday (27.2%) come from rookies - the most in the NFL. Given that, they have every reason to be elated about what they saw Sunday. Kadyn Proctor was the biggest standout with some truly elite reps in the run game. His power for a 21-year-old is special and translated vs. grown men.
Proctor with a couple pancakes & a knockdown on the 2nd level. Solid debut. Anchor looked pretty strong. Got slipped once across his face against a wide alignment. Another favorable matchup next week against SF's IDL. pic.twitter.com/eF0cvfGBX4
While I think Dolphins' other first-rounder Chris Johnson will be a fine player in time, he had an up-and-down Week 1 with a couple of pass breakups, but a couple of big plays as well. I felt similarly about second-round linebacker Jacob Rodriguez as well. While he struggled to get off the blocks consistently, you saw the play speed flash in space on numerous occasions.
The final rookie worth a mention was third-round receiver Caleb Douglas , who led all rookies with five catches for 94 yards Sunday. In a very underpowered receiving room, Douglas played with a comfort level well beyond that of a rookie.
Dolphins rookie WR Caleb Douglas moved me in week 1. Feed him more targets pic.twitter.com/nm72ms8EJ1
Highlight: Francis Mauigoa's stout pass pro Lowlight: Colton Hood only sees six snaps
Giants fans may see this as a slight, but to me, they check in fifth because I'd expect the only team with two top-10 picks to get an impact out of its rookie class. Arvell Reese was an obvious upgrade for their run defense, while Francis Mauigoa solidified their right guard spot.
There were reps from both, where you saw the high-end talent, but both looked like rookies at times, too.
Wake up with rookie Guard #65 Francis Mauigoa pic.twitter.com/VcNdfBNCCO
The cherry on top of this draft class is third-rounder Malachi Fields , who's already playing a very important role for Matt Nagy's offense. That is doing the dirty work. Fields looks like he'll be a value add in the run game with his ability to dig out box defenders from reduced splits.
Malachi Fields blocking pic.twitter.com/nXtfKRaPFi
author: Mike Renner

title: Predicting the entire NFL playoff bracket after Week 1, including a surprise Super Bowl winner
summary: A wild opening week reshaped our projected playoff bracket, with the Patriots missing out
full_text:
It might sound crazy to try and predict the entire NFL playoff field after just one week of action, but we specialize in crazy.
Week 1 turned the NFL upside down, and you can mostly blame the two teams in Los Angeles for that. The Rams were the Super Bowl favorite going into the season, but right now, it's hard to  envision them even winning their division after they got blasted 27-7 by the 49ers in Australia. And then we have the Chargers . They usually wait until the playoffs to let their fan base down, but this year, they did it in Week 1 with a stunning 26-14 loss to the Cardinals .
As if that's not enough, EVERY team in the NFC South is 0-1, making that possibly the most unpredictable division in the NFL this year. Actually, I take that back; nothing is unpredictable for us here, and that's because we have our resident analytics expert, Stephen Oh, who simulated the rest of the season to see how things will end up playing out. For those of you who are not familiar with Oh's work, let me just say this: If AI was human, it would be Oh.
They say don't overreact to Week 1, but our simulation has run the numbers and reacted accordingly. With that in mind, let's get to the projections.
Before the season started, the Chiefs were kind of a question mark, but that's not the case anymore after their dominant 31-10 win over the Broncos on Monday night. Our projection model is now feeling confident that the AFC West will go through Kansas City this year.
If this projection holds up, that means we'll have three new playoff teams in the AFC with the Ravens, Bengals and Chiefs getting in. The biggest surprise here might be that the reigning AFC champion Patriots are projected to miss the postseason.
In the NFC, the computer has three teams in the NFC West making the playoffs. Before the season started, our computer surprisingly projected the Seahawks to win the NFC West over the Rams, which looks like a smart pick right now after the way Week 1 played out. Despite their ugly loss in Week 1, the Rams are still projected to make the playoffs, but just barely. Oh, and did I mention that we have a surprise winner coming out of the NFC South? Because we have a surprise winner coming out of the NFC South.
It's almost impossible to predict who will win the NFC South, but the computer likes Atlanta. The Falcons lost to the Steelers 20-13 in Week 1, but it's a game they certainly could have won if they hadn't been forced to start a third-string QB and didn't miss two field goals.
In the NFC North, the Bears' 59-point outburst wasn't enough to put them at the top of the division. The computer still thinks the Lions are in the driver's seat.
Now that we know who's in the playoffs, let's see who's going to make it to Super Bowl LXI.
And now, we're down to our final eight teams.
Things are getting interesting. We're down to four teams, and two of them -- the Bills and Lions -- have never won a Super Bowl.
If our projection is correct, we're going to be getting a battle of the birds in the Super Bowl.
NOTE: The Seahawks have said that Sam Darnold's injury isn't serious, so the computer is assuming that Darnold will be out for a short period of time. If it turns into a longer absence, that could certainly change our projections.
author: John Breech

title: Super Bowl stock report for Week 2: 49ers are healthy and formidable, Chargers dig deeper hole
summary: We assess the NFL title race after Week 1 and identify three upcoming games that could reshape the Super Bowl picture
full_text:
You cannot win the Super Bowl in Week 1. But you can't lose it, either. You certainly can put the right or wrong foot forward on the path to the championship. Swamping the preseason favorite in Australia like the San Francisco 49ers did is about the best start possible, while losing to a team in the mix for the No. 1 draft pick a la the Los Angeles Chargers will instill zero confidence in one's ability to compete for the Vince Lombardi Trophy.
Week 1 is ripe for overreactions . Some takeaways will age poorly. What if they carry over into Week 2, though? What if the 49ers continue their hot start and take further command of the NFC West? What if the Chargers drop another game to a perceived bottom-dweller? The conversations about their respective trajectories will only grow stronger.
Each week this season, we will take a snapshot of the Super Bowl race and determine which teams are trending up, which are trending down, and which upcoming games will shake up the title race.
Here is the Super Bowl stock report heading into Week 2.
Odds via DraftKings , +2000 or better
Maybe they are not fully healthy, but even with Alfred Collins on injured reserve, Mykel Williams on the PUP list and De'Zhaun Stribling set to miss at least a month , the 49ers are far closer to full strength now than they were at essentially any point in 2025. The issue with this team has never been talent but rather the ability to keep it on the field. For now, at least, the 49ers have enough tools in their belt.
The 27-7 win over the Los Angeles Rams in Australia was not just a wire-to-wire beatdown. It was also a statement to the entire NFC. The assumption is that the team that emerges as the NFC West champion will represent the entire conference in the Super Bowl. After one week, the 49ers look like the strongest team in football's most loaded division . That is saying a lot, considering the reigning Super Bowl champions and a Rams team that just about everyone thought would cruise to the postseason.
San Francisco's defense allowed just the third-lowest EPA per play of any team in the league in Week 1, and it did so against an offense that boasts the reigning MVP. On the other side of the ball, Mike Evans ' arrival as a new weapon for Brock Purdy , Deebo Samuel's return as a proven playmaker in this offense and Kaelon Black's emergence as a capable running mate for Christian McCaffrey helped the 49ers carve up what is supposed to be one of the league's stingiest defenses.
What was supposed to be the third-best team in its own division has the makings of a squad that could get back to the Super Bowl for the third time under Kyle Shanahan.
When the NFL released the 2026 schedule, it set the Chargers up for an absolute gauntlet. Based on last year's win totals, the Chargers face the ninth-toughest slate of anyone in the league. It was vitally important for them to take advantage of two home games against projected bottom-dwellers before embarking on perhaps the most brutal eight-game stretch the league has to offer.
But they lost to the Arizona Cardinals . By 12 points. At SoFi Stadium. With two turnovers. The Cardinals never trailed in a game they went on to win, 26-14. Maybe Arizona is much better than everyone thought, and perhaps the Chargers are far worse than expected. Both things could be true.
The biggest problem for Jim Harbaugh right now is that every win in the first half of the season matters. With a schedule so grueling, he needs his team to at least tread water until December in order to have a chance at making it out of a competitive AFC West. Losing to a team that might be in the running for the No. 1 overall pick is not the right way to start.
The John Harbaugh effect is already working its magic in New York. In the Giants ' 28-20 win over the Dallas Cowboys , they displayed a heightened element of toughness on both sides of the ball, showed off a clearly improved Jaxson Dart and uncorked a new weapon in tight end Isaiah Likely , who might be the kind of X-factor that takes this offense to another level.
To be frank, the Cowboys defense might just still be terrible. That should not discount the Giants' performance too much, though. Harbaugh is as proven of a winner as nearly anyone else on the sidelines in this league and has a bevy of young talent at his disposal, and he made excellent use of it in the win -- caliber of opponent aside.
Plus, it was not just the offense that thrived on "Sunday Night Football." The Giants limited the potent Dallas offense to 20 points while containing Javonte Williams to a modest 41 yards and bottling up CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens to the tune of a combined 72. It was a multifaceted, victorious effort by the home team in Harbaugh's debut, and one that suggested the Giants might already be closer to the top of the NFC than the bottom.
The most entertaining matchup of Week 2 is the one that opens the slate. The new Highmark Stadium will be rocking in its inaugural regular-season game. That is one of the three contests with the greatest Super Bowl implications this week.
Scoreboard operator, get ready for a busy day. The Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions both had their Week 1 games decided in the 30s, and that will likely be a trend for them all year, with two of the NFL's most talent-laden offenses and defenses that, though it was just one game, seem as shaky as they did a year ago. Both enter this Thursday night battle at 1-0, and once the contest is done, one team will boast two wins over postseason contenders right out of the gate.
The mighty Houston Texans defense could not have drawn two tougher matchups to open the year. It failed its first test in the loss to the Bills and now faces another one with Joe Burrow and Ja'Marr Chase coming to town. There is no reason to believe that the NFL's most powerful defense is all of a sudden anything less than elite, but a second consecutive head-scratcher to open the year would cause at least a little bit of doubt to creep in. On the other side, the reworked Cincinnati Bengals defense has an opportunity against C.J. Stroud to prove that last week's promising effort was no fluke.
There is a lot to be learned about the Jacksonville Jaguars ' upcoming trip to the Mile High City. Are they really as good as they looked against the Cleveland Browns , or was their opponent just as bad as they come? And for the Denver Broncos, are there legitimate concerns, or did their Monday night loss say more about the Kansas City Chiefs being back than anything else? It is a step up in competition for the Jaguars and a spot where the Broncos need to get right. An 0-2 hole for Denver would raise a few early-season alarms as they seek a return to the AFC title game.
author: Carter Bahns

title: From walk-on at North Texas to promising NFL Draft prospect: What early season says about QB Drew Mestemaker
summary: After a 426-yard breakout performance against Oregon, former North Texas transfer Drew Mestemaker is rapidly rising in early 2027 NFL Draft evaluations
full_text:
The college football and NFL Draft communities alike are enamored with a former walk-on quarterback from Austin, Texas. No, this is not a repackaged story on Baker Mayfield, but rather Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker.
CBS Sports' Shehan Jeyarajah wrote an excellent story detailing the Texas native's journey from earning district recognition as both a safety and punter, but never taking a varsity snap at quarterback to now being one of the hottest names at the quarterback position ahead of the 2027 NFL Draft.
Mestemaker's Cowboys have had an unorthodox start to the season; first falling to in-state Tulsa and then knocking off No. 6 Oregon. Each game provided evidence of both the player's strengths and weaknesses. What does the scouting report say about his draft prospects? I solicited the opinion of retired old man soccer star and CBS Sports NFL Draft analyst Ryan Wilson for his thoughts on the quarterback captivating audiences.
"Coming into the season, I was just working from the assumption that Drew Mestemaker would return to school for the 2027 season. Now … maybe not?
"That was my point of reference when I watched him over the summer; he was coming off a huge 2025 season at North Texas, but he had only 13 career starts, hadn't faced a Power 4 opponent and still looked like a quarterback who would probably benefit from another year of development. I had him as my QB9 back in August and while there was plenty to like -- he could work through reads from a clean pocket and consistently showed good touch on intermediate throws -- I also had questions about the arm strength, not always playing on time and occasionally locking onto his first read and forcing the issue.
"Over the summer, I came up with the First-Round Readiness Score (let's call it FRED) to measure a quarterback's current development against the traits and production of past first-rounders. Let's just say the model was considerably more bullish on Mestemaker than my notes . His combination of production, efficiency and early career development gave him one of the strongest scores in the class, behind only Julian Sayin and Jayden Maiava -- and well ahead of Oregon's Dante Moore and Texas' Arch Manning.
"FRED was essentially telling me that I might be underselling how far along he already was," Wilson said.
Speaking to my personal summer process, Mestemaker was a top 50 overall prospect, but clustered in Tier 2 behind Arch Manning, Moore and South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers.
First and foremost, the NFL game is changing. There is less of an emphasis on a quarterback's ability to run the football and more of an emphasis on operating on time and making quick, accurate decisions as a passer from the pocket. Mestemaker has the foot speed to get chunk yardage on the ground, as was seen against Oregon, but is more of a straight-line sprinter than a sudden athlete who will put defenders in compromised positions in space.
His pocket presence was a bit up and down last season but he stood tall in the face of pressure. Mestemaker makes quick decisions and throws with touch, anticipation to allow pass catchers the opportunity to make plays post-catch.
One of the biggest question marks had been how he would handle the transition to Power 4 competition. In two years with the Mean Green, his only exposure to that level of competition had been three pass attempts against Texas Tech in a 66-21 loss.
Fast forward to September when he made his first two starts at Oklahoma State alongside 53 other incoming transfers, including 15 former teammates from North Texas.
"Mestemaker's Oklahoma State debut against Tulsa didn't do much to change my mind. He had some rough moments, struggled to push the ball downfield and looked like a quarterback still adjusting to a new offense. No real surprise and also no reason to panic.
Then Oregon happened," Wilson continued.
"In his first start against a Power 4 team, Mestemaker finished with 426 total yards and outplayed Moore by a wide margin. And some of the things I wanted to see from him showed up in that game. His arm looked stronger than it did last season. He ripped intermediate field-size throws on time, showed great touch and timing on deep balls in the face of pressure and looked a lot like Josh Allen, his favorite player growing up, when he decided to run.
"His footwork from a clean pocket was especially encouraging. He also showed he could play on the move, throwing with pace and accuracy, and Oklahoma State trusted him with the ball on a third-down QB keeper to seal the win.
"There are still reasons to exercise patience. Oregon's defense was, to put it politely, awful. Mestemaker can panic when the first read disappears, and he'll still miss easy throws when his feet aren't set or stare down a target long enough to bring underneath defenders into the play.
So this isn't suddenly a QB1 conversation . But the question has changed, for sure. Before the season, I was wondering whether Mestemaker, who is just 20 years old, would show enough to make himself a legitimate 2028 prospect. Two games in, it's fair to wonder if he might force his way into the 2027 QB conversation."
Through two games, Mestemaker has been pressured on 32.3% of dropbacks, according to TruMedia. On average, he is being pressured once for every three drop backs. There was a discomfort evident against Tulsa. He consistently had pressure in his armpit and was unnecessarily fading away from throws. There were a number of errant throws that were a byproduct of poor footwork and not opening his hips to the throw.
Against Oregon, he displayed better pocket presence as well as the arm strength and decisiveness to rip the ball over the middle of the field. When forced out of the pocket, he struggles to reset his feet.
CBS Sports' Mike Renner has him as the No. 9 overall prospect . Although I am not yet personally as high on the player, there is cautious optimism that he will factor into first-round conversations if he continues on this trajectory.
The Ducks represented arguably the stiffest competition on Oklahoma State's schedule. They have just one more ranked meeting at No. 22 Houston before traveling to Lubbock to play No. 13 Texas Tech Nov. 14.
author: Josh Edwards

title: Mike Tomlin invokes infamous 'Browns is the Browns' line after Cleveland loss, Todd Monken responds
summary: Tomlin used his NBC debut to take a familiar shot at his former AFC North rival, prompting new Browns coach Todd Monken to push back
full_text:
A healthy list of NFL teams disappointed in the first week of the 2026 season. The New England Patriots and Green Bay Packers lost to backup quarterbacks, the Denver Broncos couldn't make a tackle, and the Tennessee Titans couldn't do anything right. Then, there are the Cleveland Browns .
The Browns fell to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Todd Monken's coaching debut, 34-10, and the game went the way many thought it would, with Cleveland a two-score underdog. The defense struggled to contain Jags quarterback Trevor Lawrence , who completed 18 of 23 passes for 245 yards and four touchdowns, while Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson threw for 205 yards, one touchdown and one interception while taking five sacks.
Cleveland recorded 272 yards of total offense and didn't score a point until the second half. With this loss, the Browns fell to 3-24-1 in Week 1s since 1999, and Watson faced the largest deficit (31 points) of his Browns career -- which consists of 20 starts.
Former Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike Tomlin didn't have much to say about the Browns' Week 1 performance during his debut on "Football Night in America" on NBC, but he did shout out one of his former players for a famous quote that continues to live on.
"In the words of my friend JuJu Smith-Schuster , the Browns is the Browns," Tomlin said.
Mike Tomlin: "In the words of my friend JuJu Smith-Schuster, the Browns is the Browns."  🏈💀🎙️ pic.twitter.com/5jRJYeRgG1
Back in 2021, Smith-Schuster was asked about the Steelers' rivalry with the Browns. He indicated that nothing really changes with Cleveland's organization no matter how many new coaches or players they bring in.
"I think they're still the same Browns teams I play every year," Smith-Schuster said, via the Associated Press . "I think they're nameless gray faces. They have a couple good players on their team, but at the end of the day, I don't know. The Browns is the Browns."
Tomlin is probably allowed to take shots at his old rival. After all, he went 28-9-1 in the regular season against Cleveland.
There is some truth to JuJu's blunt assessment. The Browns registered just four winning seasons since 1999, and won one playoff game. Still, Monken isn't prepared to embrace the ghosts of Cleveland's past. He disagreed with Tomlin's assessment.
"Everybody's afforded their opinions. That's what you do when you go from coaching to television," Monken said. "We have to own that. We have to own that. We didn't play very well. I don't see it that way, 'Browns being Browns.' I don't see it that way. Every week is different, every team is different. We just didn't play well. That's one week. That's not 'Browns being Browns,' that's Browns being poorly on one week...
"The only way to change people's opinions is to play better. That's a fact."
There are not many reasons to be optimistic about the Browns right now, but Monken is correct. Winning cures everything, and Cleveland's next chance to win is on the road this week against Baker Mayfield and the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
author: Jordan Dajani

title: 2026 NFL Week 2 injury panic meter: Myles Garrett, A.J. Brown, Sam Darnold sidelined with lower body issues
summary: Gauging the outlook for some of the league's biggest Week 1 injuries
full_text:
The 2026 NFL season is in full tilt with Week 1 in the books, but unfortunately that also means the injuries that come with playing the violent game that is professional football are also back in our lives.
The biggest-name offseason acquisitions -- Los Angeles Rams All-Pro edge rusher Myles Garrett and New England Patriots Pro Bowl wide receiver A.J. Brown -- are sidelined for multiple weeks and plenty of other high-impact contributors were injured on Sunday. Which players will be placed on injured reserve for at least a month? Who will fight to get back on the field after a week or two? Who will look to return in Week 2?
We've gathered the biggest early-season injuries from around the league, and we'll be evaluating each injury situation with a panic meter as listed below:
Los Angeles will be without the 2025 NFL Defensive Player of the Year for an extended amount of time, which is a big deal. Garrett missed most of training camp, including a joint practice against the Dallas Cowboys , with swelling in his knee. The Rams, head coach Sean McVay and Garrett, thought he could power through the injury in Week 1 against the San Francisco 49ers , but that obviously didn't come to fruition. Garrett produced just his fourth career game without a tackle on 39 defensive snaps and his first since Week 11 of the 2024 season.
Now, he's headed for knee surgery.
"Thought we would take an approach where he'd be feeling good enough to go contribute positive change and be the player that he's capable of," McVay said Monday, via ESPN . "That wasn't the case. And so the next right thing for us is to be able to get this thing fixed."
Los Angeles placed him on injured reserve, which means he will be out at least four games, and McVay said there won't be a timeline for Garrett's absence until after the surgery on Monday. The Rams head coach said the decision for him to have surgery came shortly after speaking with Garrett and seeing his on-field limitations. He looked like a shell of the player who racked up an NFL single-season record 23.0 sacks just last season. Garrett admitted he wasn't playing freely and was thinking about how to move to stay healthy. That's why the surgery is happening.
"When I was out there, I was a little bit more focused on myself and trying to stay healthy than what they were doing, and that showed," Garrett said. "I wasn't who I needed to be for my team."
There are a few reasons why the panic level is high for Garrett. One reason is that he's a generational, physical specimen, so for him of all people to not be able to overcome an injury, that means it's pretty bad. Two, the Rams could not be more all in for the 2026 season than they are right now. Future Hall of Famer Aaron Donald came out of retirement on a one-year deal to play with Donald. In addition to Donald, the following key contributors are free agents next offseason: wide receiver Davante Adams , center Coleman Shelton , cornerback Emmanuel Forbes , guard Steve Avila , edge rusher Byron Young , defensive tackle Kobie Turner , wide receiver Puka Nacua and kicker Harrison Mevis .
Los Angeles can't afford to not have Garrett out for long while playing in an NFC West with the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks , a San Francisco 49ers team that just smoked them in Week 1 and an Arizona Cardinals team that could be surprisingly feisty after beating the Los Angeles Chargers at SoFi Stadium on Sunday. A prolonged absence could lead to the Rams scratching and clawing just to be a wild card team. Plus, Garrett is on the wrong side of 30 years old now. He'll be 31 years old on Dec. 29.
Garrett is a generational freak, but this injury shows there's no guarantee the Rams will be getting the superhero-level production they were banking on in 2026   when they traded away Pro Bowl edge rusher Jared Verse , their 2027 first-round, 2028 second-round pick and 2029 third-round pick.
Three-time Pro Bowl wide receiver A.J. Brown didn't survive his first game as the New England Patriots' No. 1 target, suffering a high right ankle sprain in Week 1 at the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Now, Brown is on injured reserve, which means he is out at least four games.
The panic is high because the Patriots' passing offense looked completely lost against Seattle, albeit one of the league's best defenses, without Brown. Romeo Doubs , the ex-Green Bay Packers receiver New England signed on a four-year, $68 million contract with $39 million guarantee this offseason, struggled mightily, going without a catch on three targets including a drop. That drop then led to one of quarterback Drake Maye 's career-high three interceptions a play later.
New England's offense could end up stuck in the mud without Brown the next month or so since they don't really have another target who can take the top off a defense on deep, downfield routes. Trading away deep threat Kayshon Boutte prior to the start of the 2026 season feels incredibly shortsighted at the moment.
Seattle two-time Pro Bowl quarterback Sam Darnold suffered a nebulous hip injury on the Seahawks' opening drive of the new season. ESPN reports Darnold has a "very unique" soft-tissue injury that didn't actually cause structural damage to his hip joint. It's worrisome that he doesn't have a recovery timeline established just yet, but the Seahawks reportedly expect his time on the sidelines will be short.
A medium panic level makes sense here because of the uncertainty for when Darnold returns, but Drew Lock has shown he is capable of holding the fort. Lock should be able to do just that over the next two weeks at the Arizona Cardinals and the Washington Commanders .
The hit from Packers safety Javon Bullard that caused Minnesota Vikings two-time Pro Bowl quarterback Kyler Murray 's concussion looked bad, but head coach Kevin O'Connell said on Monday that Murray is able to participate in meetings. The team is taking Murray's health as day-by-day while he goes through the steps of the NFL's concussion protocol, but they honestly don't need to rush him back.
Murray panicked on his first throw against the Green Bay Packers, heaving a lollipop into double coverage on a blitz that resulted in an interception. Plus, Carson Wentz put together a historic performance off the benching, throwing for 133 yards and 3 passing touchdowns on 12 of 19 passing. That made him just the second player in the Super Bowl era with three-plus passing touchdowns off the bench in a winning effort in a season opener along with Carolina Panthers quarterback Jake Delhomme back in 2003, per CBS Sports Research. Minnesota has no need to rush Murray back. If Wentz thrives against the Chicago Bears in Week 2, then there's a quarterback conversation to be had. If not, then Murray will likely be able to pass through concussion protocol by Week 3.
Scary scene as Kyler Murray takes a massive hit and stays down after the play. pic.twitter.com/sVqZ7M24e4
The news that Las Vegas Raiders All-Pro tight end Brock Bowers underwent a meniscus trim surgical procedure the Tuesday before Week 1 was shocking. Even more shocking is that ESPN is reporting Bowers is projected to miss just "a game or two" after he dealt with a knee strain and a PCL injury in 2025.
Panic here is medium because Bowers' history of knee injuries is seemingly becoming a trend. However, the return timeline is short. Las Vegas is in wait-and-see mode, but it feels like there's a chance the Raiders could do a little more waiting than just a couple games.
Baltimore Ravens two-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Zay Flowers erupted for a career-high 150 yards receiving and a receiving touchdown all in the first half of the Ravens' 41-23 demolition of the Indianapolis Colts . The reason he didn't produce anything more after halftime is because he was ruled out with a hamstring injury.
The good news is Ravens head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Monday that Flowers is simply "day to day." That's a major relief for Baltimore…
author: Garrett Podell

title: Prisco's NFL Week 2 Power Rankings: Rams and Cowboys get a wake-up call, 49ers on the rise
summary: Pete Prisco shares his Week 2 Power Rankings, including the Bears, Giants and Cardinals moving up
full_text:
The Los Angeles Rams are done.
The Carolina Panthers ' defense is awful.
The Chicago Bears will break the single-season scoring record.
The Houston Texans ' vaunted defense is now a sieve.
Same for the Denver Broncos .
The Dallas Cowboys are toast.
The Green Bay Packers won't ever hold a lead.
On and on it goes. The Week 1 overreaction bucket is full. Don't be guilty of buying into any of it.
Be more like NFL coaches talking to their teams today: It's just one week. Move on.
Week 1 is full of teases over the years. Remember when the Las Vegas Raiders went to Foxborough and beat the New England Patriots in Week 1 last year. All the Pats did was get to the Super Bowl , while the Raiders were a season-long disaster in 2025.
So don't fall victim to the overreactions.
I took that into account when doing my Week 2 Power Rankings. The Seattle Seahawks stay in the top spot after beating the Patriots to open the season, while the 49ers have moved up after blowing out the Rams. The Rams fall -- but not too far.
That doesn't mean there aren't changes. How can the Los Angeles Chargers not fall after losing at home to the Arizona Cardinals ? The Dallas Cowboys looked terrible on defense Sunday night in losing to the Giants , so they drop a few.
I just want to be cautious that one week won't greatly impact my rankings. One thing that didn't change is Miami in the bottom spot. The Dolphins didn't look good in their loss to the Raiders, but the Cleveland Browns and Tennessee Titans have the look of teams that will challenge Miami all year long for the cellar.
Then agin, it's just one week.

title: Falcons’ starting QB for Sunday vs. Panthers still undecided
summary: The Falcons’ quarterback situation seems even murkier after head coach Kevin Stefanski spoke to the media on Wednesday. But Stefanski said he isn’t frustrated. “We want to be able to win and play well regardless of who’s in,” Stefanski said, and saying that the frustration actually comes from losing and falling short on the field. […]
full_text: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Falcons’ quarterback situation seems even murkier after head coach Kevin Stefanski spoke to the media on Wednesday. But Stefanski said he isn’t frustrated. “We want to be able to win and play well regardless of who’s in,” Stefanski said, and saying that the frustration actually comes from losing and falling short on the field. Cooper Rush will practice fully on Wednesday, per Stefanski. I’d expect Rush to remain on the injury report today as he is still getting treatment on his back. “Not many guys are 100% coming out of Week 1,” Stefanski said. Tua Tagovailoa will not practice on Wednesday, but Stefanski said Tua is “getting better.” We didn’t hear anything new from Stefanski on Michael Penix — he’s still progressing and the team and medical staff are happy with the progress, but there is no timetable for him to take over as the starter. And Stefanski declined to rule any quarterback out for Week 2’s home opener against the Carolina Panthers. Yes, that does create the possibility for Jack Strand to see some action on Sunday. Bijan Robinson also spoke to the media before practice, and he shared that it is a little challenging to not know who’s starting at quarterback on Sunday — and the fact that Tua and Penix are both lefties and Rush is right-handed is an additional wrinkle. If they’re designing this game plan around Rush, and they decide Friday that Tua will be the starter, it changes the direction of each play. But it doesn’t matter to Bijan who starts at quarterback — even if it means a LOT of touches like he had against the Steelers in Week 1. “We have so many great playmakers on the offense,” says Bijan. “…for me, it’s whatever I can do to help my team win the game.” And the skill players have to bring the energy and focus to prep this week so they’re prepared for anything, Bijan said. I’m still expecting Rush to start on Sunday against the Panthers, but I’d love to be surprised by Tua, or even better, by Penix.

The team has promoted tight end Nick Muse to the 53 man roster in a corresponding move and have added defensive end Drake Jackson and running back Khalil Herbert to the practice squad. The Atlanta Falcons have officially placed DT Da'Shawn Hand on injured reserve. They've signed TE Nick Muse to the active roster to fill Hand's spot. They've also filled out their practice squad by signing DE Drake Jackson and RB Khalil Herbert. https://t.co/rNd9evFFWs — Will McFadden (@willmcfadden) September 16, 2026 We wrote about Hand the other day , but suffice to say his injury is devastating given that the team was set to rely on him as a run-stopping early down force in the middle of this defense. The Falcons will have to replace him by committee but may still sign another player, given that their defensive front is talented but perhaps not as deep as we’d like early in the season. Muse earned the call-up by playing a ton on special teams against Pittsburgh and looking good both in that phase and in his limited looks as a blocker, the same as he has all summer. The Falcons are going to lean heavily on tight ends to help keep either Cooper Rush or Tua Tagovailoa alive in the first weeks of the season, and Muse figures to get some run as part of that mission. Jackson was a former second round pick for the 49ers who had three sacks in each of his first two seasons working as a reserve, but has seen his career spectacularly derailed by injuries that cost him half the 2023 season, the entire 2024 season, and much of the 2025 season. He was released by the Commanders, who picked him up in 2025, with an injury settlement earlier this year. If he’s healthy, he offers some experience and potential upside on the practice squad, as Jackson is still just 25 years old. I mentioned Herbert as a candidate for this roster way back in March , noting that he’s been a pretty productive player when he’s had opportunities, can catch the ball, and has returned kicks. With Tyler Goodson headed to Dallas, Atlanta needed a veteran third back and I think Herbert fits the bill quite well. We’ll see if he’s elevated this week. Join me in giving Muse his props for the elevation, welcoming Herbert and Jackson, and wishing Hand well on his recovery.

title: Falcons Week 1 3 up and 3 down: Defense is up, Offense is down
summary: The Atlanta Falcons couldn’t bring home the win in the season opener, but it wasn’t due to the defensive performances we saw. Unfortunately, the offense and special teams unit let the team down, a story many fans are tired of hearing. Here’s the Week 1, 3 up and 3 down: 3 up Sydney Brown Acquiring […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers is sacked by Za'darius Smith #91 of the Atlanta Falcons during the fourth quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Atlanta Falcons couldn’t bring home the win in the season opener, but it wasn’t due to the defensive performances we saw. Unfortunately, the offense and special teams unit let the team down, a story many fans are tired of hearing. Here’s the Week 1, 3 up and 3 down: 3 up Sydney Brown Falcons DB Sydney Brown was flying around. Showed that he can be a legit 3rd safety/overhang and make plays for you in the box. Falcons struggled with tackling in the secondary last year and Brown limited YAC opportunities yesterday. pic.twitter.com/ovudZnJ65y — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) September 14, 2026 Acquiring Brown was one of Ian Cunningham’s first moves as GM, and it’s already shaping up to be one of his best. When Brown signed, the initial thought was that he’d be a good special teams contributor and competent depth, but Jeff Ulbrich had bigger plans. Brown was more than depth in the season opener; he was essentially a starter, logging 30 snaps and making every one count. Brown was a force in the box, blowing up runs without fear and getting ball carriers on the ground almost immediately. He also blew up the screen play that led to a fumble recovery. It’s going to be fun to see how his role evolves on this defense, because he’s making it tough to keep him off the field. Za’Darius Smith Expectations were low for Smith entering Week 1; he was ready to call it a career and joined the team late. Smith blew those expectations out of the water. On just 16 snaps , he logged 2 sacks, providing the defense with the finisher they desperately needed after losing both Jalon Walker and James Pearce Jr. Smith’s role is expected to grow as the season progresses, but getting production out of him this early on a limited snap count is hopefully a sign of even better things to come for the veteran. Maason Smith Smith was acquired in a player-for-player trade involving Ruke Orhorhoro. The initial take was that this was a lemon swap between two franchises disappointed with their 2nd-round investments. One man’s trash is another man’s treasure. Smith was a force early, splitting double teams and pushing the pocket. If not for a questionable penalty, he would’ve finished the afternoon with a sack. Atlanta has needed a physical presence in the middle of their front, and while it’s too early to say the problem is officially solved, this performance brings the team one step closer to checking that box. Falcons new DT Maason Smith had a nice debut pic.twitter.com/rytlVqKfww — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) September 14, 2026 3 down Matthew Bergeron It was a middling effort for the Falcons offensive line overall, but when you’re the highest-paid member, the spotlight will always be on you. Many questioned the price tag attached to Bergeron’s extension, and those questions still linger after this week’s performance. The left guard committed two holding penalties after getting beat clean off the snap. He also blew an assignment when pulling to the backside of the run, resulting in a negative play. There were flashes of good play but not enough to justify the new deal. Jake Matthews and Chris Lindstrom also had off days, so the hope is this was just the group still adjusting to the new scheme. Nick Folk The most accurate kicker from 2025 doubled his miss count in the 2026 opener. The 54-yard miss is somewhat understandable; at his age, that could be just outside of his range. However, the 45-yard miss was inexcusable. Yes, Pittsburgh is a notoriously difficult place to kick, but when the team signed Folk, it was with the expectation that he would be able to overcome those difficult environments. We aren’t hitting the panic button yet; Folk finished 2/4 on the day, but fans will be feeling a little less confident when he steps on the field for the next few games. Cooper Rush Rush was thrust into the starting role after Tua Tagovailoa was downgraded with an oblique strain. Rush then started experiencing back spasms the day before the game, and looked uncomfortable from the first snap. It was clear that the ball wasn’t getting aired out in this matchup, and even completing simple screens became a monumental task. It was interesting to see he had success on the few play-action concepts run Sunday, and if he’s starting again in Week 2, Rees needs to lean into those concepts more if he wants to salvage the passing game. The #Falcons ran 3 Playaction plays all from under center against the Steelers imo not just Cooper but the entire offense looked comfortable. Cooper had a 26.1% successfull play rate/ -1.07 epa on plays with no PA vs a 100% success rate/ +2.00 epa pic.twitter.com/EUH5xqLoMY — Juke🔴⚫️⚪️ (@Jukejuke99) September 15, 2026 While the Falcons didn’t get the win, all hope isn’t lost. This defense has legitimate pieces that will keep the Falcons in games all season. If the offense and special teams can pull their weight, this team can win games this year. The team will host the Carolina Panthers in Week 2, who’ve had the Falcons number lately.

title: Cooper Rush seems likely to start at QB for Falcons vs. Panthers in Week 2

It’s not an announcement, it hasn’t been confirmed by the team — […]
full_text: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We’ll know for certain on Wednesday. But there was a change to the Falcons media availability schedule for this week that hit my inbox Tuesday morning, and the “starting QB” press conference scheduled for Wednesday now has Cooper Rush’s name in that slot. It’s not an announcement, it hasn’t been confirmed by the team — but it seems pretty obvious that’s the direction we’re heading. We should also get updates on Wednesday from Stefanski on Michael Penix’s status and Tua Tagovailoa’s back, as well as the back issues Rush seemed to still be dealing with during Sunday’s loss to the Steelers. Could the plan at starting quarterback change over the course of the week? The quarterback depth chart has been such a wild ride since the beginning of camp, so nothing would surprise me at this point. For those of you on the Jack Strand-wagon, I’m sure we’ll hear more from Stefanski Wednesday on how the rookie UDFA fits into the team’s plans, now and into the future. They seem high on him, but any UDFA out of a small program is going to need significant development. Strand is athletically gifted, and he’s also brilliant. His learning curve should be shorter as a result, but it still exists. As our fearless leader Dave Choate likes to say, it’s time to gird our loins and start preparing for whatever surprises the Atlanta Falcons quarterback depth chart has in store for us this week. Hopefully one of those surprises will be a divisional win over the Panthers on Sunday.

title: AFC North Week 1 Recap
summary: Baltimore Beatdown’s weekly AFC North recap is back. Every week, Dustin Cox will be bringing you the highlights around the division – so you don’t have to spend any time watching the Browns! Baltimore Ravens (1-0) The Jesse Minter era started strong for the Ravens as they blew past the Indianapolis Colts, 41-23. Minter’s defense was […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 13: Deshaun Watson #4 of the Cleveland Browns throws a pass against the Jacksonville Jaguars during the third quarter of the game at EverBank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Don Juan Moore/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Beatdown’s weekly AFC North recap is back. Every week, Dustin Cox will be bringing you the highlights around the division – so you don’t have to spend any time watching the Browns! Baltimore Ravens (1-0) The Jesse Minter era started strong for the Ravens as they blew past the Indianapolis Colts, 41-23. Minter’s defense was as advertised in Week 1, limiting big plays through the air, applying consistent pressure on the quarterback, and forcing two turnovers. Baltimore’s big-ticket free-agent signing, Trey Hendrickson, led the way up front with eight pressures, while Tavius Robinson and Malaki Starks each had a sack. Roquan Smith and Marlon Humphrey, two highly paid veterans looking to rebound from down seasons, caused the two turnovers with an interception and forced fumble, respectively. Declan Doyle’s offense lived up to the hype with 506 total yards on the day. Lamar Jackson looked as good as ever, completing 17 of 25 passes for 324 yards and a touchdown, with 40 rushing yards and another score on the ground. Zay Flowers was unstoppable in the first half, racking up a career-high 150 yards and a touchdown before leaving the game with a hamstring injury. Derrick Henry appears poised for another monster season after tallying 144 rushing yards and three touchdowns on 24 carries against the Colts. Cincinnati Bengals (1-0) The Bengals started their season with a 33-27 win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Cincinnati revamped their defense this offseason, and the unit wasted no time showing their improvement with four turnovers against the Buccaneers. The Bengals forced three fumbles against Baker Mayfield while sacking him four times. Cincinnati traded a first-round pick for Dexter Lawrence this offseason, and while he did not show up on the stat sheet, the massive nose tackle’s presence was certainly felt in the interior on Sunday, against both the run and pass. Joe Burrow completed 25 of 35 passes for 254 yards, a touchdown, and a pick-six in his first outing of the year. Superstar receiver Ja’Marr Chase was quiet, catching just two passes for 12 yards. Instead, veteran tight end Mike Gesicki led the team with 78 receiving yards and a touchdown on five catches. Chase Brown led the ground attack with 56 yards and a score on 16 carries, to go with another 22 yards on five receptions. Pittsburgh Steelers (1-0) Mike McCarthy’s first game as head coach of the Steelers resulted in a 20-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Cooper Rush got the start at quarterback for the Falcons in place of the injured Tua Tagovailoa, which went how you would expect against Pittsburgh’s defense. The veteran backup was picked off twice, including a pick-six by T.J. Watt. The 32-year-old pass rusher showed he’s still a game-wrecking force with two sacks as well. Safety Jaquan Brisker hauled in the team’s other interception. Aaron Rodgers’ self-proclaimed final season began on Sunday with 221 yards and a touchdown while completing 24 of 40 passes. Newly acquired wide receiver Michael Pittman led the team with 58 receiving yards on three receptions, while tight end Pat Freiermuth caught the lone touchdown. Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle nearly split carries in the backfield, with Warren leading the way with 46 rushing yards to just 15 for Dowdle. Cleveland Browns (0-1) Todd Monken’s NFL head coaching debut did not go well as the Browns fell 34-10 to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Cleveland’s defense, in their first game since trading away superstar edge rusher Myles Garrett, could not stop quarterback Trevor Lawrence. The former first-overall pick had his way through the air, completing 18 of 23 pass attempts for 245 yards and four touchdowns while being sacked just once by defensive tackle Mason Graham. Jared Verse, the budding star outside linebacker acquired as part of the Garrett trade to the Los Angeles Rams, was held in check in his debut with his new team. The Browns’ offense did not fare any better. Deshaun Watson entered the season as the starting quarterback after competing with Shedeur Sanders for the job in the offseason. Watson’s performance against the Jaguars has already led to calls for a switch at the position. He finished with 16 completions on 22 attempts for a touchdown and an interception while being sacked five times and fumbling once. Rookie first-round receiver KC Concepcion caught four passes for 43 yards while coughing up a fumble. Fellow rookie wideout Denzel Boston led the team with 59 yards and a touchdown on just two catches. The second-rounder’s 46-yard touchdown was the biggest highlight of the day for Cleveland.

author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens open as heavy favorites in potential Week 2 trap game vs. Saints
summary: The Baltimore Ravens dominated the Indianapolis Colts to start their 2026 season, so it is no surprise that they are 8.5-point favorites in Week 2 (via FanDuel Sportsbook). But the New Orleans Saints put up a surprising fight against the Detroit Lions in Week 1, losing by just one point in overtime. What looked like […]
full_text: Sep 13, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Baltimore Ravens safety Kyle Hamilton (14) takes the field to face the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Baltimore Ravens dominated the Indianapolis Colts to start their 2026 season, so it is no surprise that they are 8.5-point favorites in Week 2 ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ). But the New Orleans Saints put up a surprising fight against the Detroit Lions in Week 1, losing by just one point in overtime. What looked like a Week 2 cakewalk against an NFC South team when schedules were released now could now be an early-season trap game. Let’s set the scene. The Ravens are returning home from Indianapolis, where they just began the Jesse Minter era with an emphatic 41-23 victory against a franchise hated by fans in Baltimore. Lamar Jackson looked like a three-time MVP, Derrick Henry rumbled all game long, and the defense forced two turnovers that led to offensive scores. Special teams delivered, too, anchored by strong return units and a perfect seven-for-seven game from Tyler Loop. The team has plenty of reasons to be confident heading into their Week 2 matchup with the Saints. But New Orleans dropped 469 yards on Detroit’s defense on Sunday and converted 10 of their 19 third and fourth down attempts. They also scored in four of their five red zone trips and all four goal-to-go situations, which was a particular weakness of the Ravens defense in Indy. But Baltimore’s secondary is far better than Detroit’s, which allowed Tyler Shough to throw for 378 yards but also notched two interceptions. The Lions also sacked him five times. Defensively, the Saints could not stop Jahmyr Gibbs on the ground – a good sign for Baltimore, who could lean on their rushing attack if Zay Flowers is sidelined. But Jared Goff averaged just 5.1 yards per passing attempt and the Lions struggled to get their receivers free for yards after the catch. To be clear, the Ravens should still win this game handily. But they cannot take any opponent lightly, a trap into which past John Harbaugh squads often fell. Postgame comments from Kyle Hamilton and Jesse Minter’s Monday press conference indicate that the team is laser-focused on their next task at hand. Hamilton graded the defense’s performance as a “C-plus” in the locker room. When asked about a special celebration for Minter’s first win, he simply replied, “We get to play the Saints next week.” “I love that,” Minter said on Monday when asked about his star safety’s grade. “Look, we have capabilities of being really good. We didn’t start the way we wanted to. We responded really well. We can play a lot better in the red zone, and a lot of that is with me and some of the things that we were doing. So, we are just chasing the best version of us.” Later, Minter said he felt the defense “let the [Colts] off the hook…in the red zone.” Players and coaches could get asked about a potential trap game this week at the podium, and expect a similar line of response. Every team in the NFL is a threat – this is the league of Any Given Sunday. Vegas lines mean nothing once the ball is snapped (if they mean anything in the first place).
author: Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens vs Colts: the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly
summary: Another season of Baltimore Ravens football has kicked off, which means it’s time to get back to finding the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly in every matchup! Sunday’s win over the Colts featured plenty to be excited about, but a handful of rough moments, too. Let’s dive in! The Good Lamar Jackson: It had […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 13: Lamar Jackson #8 of the Baltimore Ravens runs the ball against the Indianapolis Colts during the second quarter of the game at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Andy Lyons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another season of Baltimore Ravens football has kicked off, which means it’s time to get back to finding the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly in every matchup! Sunday’s win over the Colts featured plenty to be excited about, but a handful of rough moments, too. Let’s dive in! The Good Lamar Jackson: It had been 252 days since the world got to see Lamar Jackson play football, and he didn’t disappoint in his return. He had over 300 yards through the air with a 124.2 passer rating. He also added another 40 yards on the ground and answered any questions about his legs with a magical sack escape and scramble to pick up a first down on 3rd and 16 that led to a touchdown. Basically, the MVP is back. The three-headed monster: The Ravens officially have a mythical creature in Baltimore. Pair Lamar Jackson’s performance with Derrick Henry’s 144 yards at 6.0 yards a pop and three touchdowns with Zay Flowers’ 150 yards and a score on five catches, and you have one of the best trios in the NFL. And Flowers’ numbers came in just the first half alone. In offensive coordinator Declan Doyle's first game as a playcaller, the Ravens produced the first game in their 31-year history with this trifecta: 🏈 300-yard passer (Lamar Jackson) 🏈 150-yard receiver (Zay Flowers) 🏈 100-yard rusher (Derrick Henry) Source: ESPN Research — Jamison Hensley (@jamisonhensley) September 14, 2026 Run game: As mentioned above, Henry was able to come in and control this game for Baltimore once they built up a lead. That was massive with Flowers out for the second half, which slowed the passing game. As the Ravens operate from under center more this year, it should open Henry to work in what he was best at in Tennessee, stretch/zone concepts that get him moving on a track. The run game is definitely where the offensive line shined too. According to Next Gen Stats, Henry wasn’t tackled behind the line of scrimmage once during the Colts game. The Ravens' offensive line needs to clean up the penalties and improve in pass protection, but the run blocking was very strong. Derrick Henry finished with 110 yards before contact against the Colts, the third-highest single-game total of his career, per @NextGenStats . Henry… — Ryan Mink (@ryanmink) September 14, 2026 Defense: Since Jesse Minter was hired, the talk around town was how much the Ravens defense would improve after the Zach Orr years. The unit proceeded to get walked down the field on their first drive of the season, and the fear started creeping back in, just slightly. But as expected, Minter adjusted, the players recovered, and Baltimore’s defense dominated the rest of the game. Daniel Jones had fewer than 200 passing yards despite trailing for most of the game. Jonathan Taylor had a solid game, but the Ravens didn’t let him break away for any massive plays. Marlon Humphrey also pried the ball out of his hands after one catch, one of Baltimore’s two turnovers along with a Roquan Smith interception. The pass rush was also very solid, as they finished with two sacks and nine quarterback hits. #Colts QB Daniel Jones was the most pressured quarterback of Week 1, according to @NextGenStats . Jones was pressured on 18 of his 34 dropbacks (52.9%) against the Ravens. — Noah Compton (@nerlens_) September 14, 2026 Special teams: My preseason worries about Tyler Loop were loud, so I’ll make this section just as loud. The second-year kicker had a fantastic day to open the season. He hit all five of his extra points and went 2/2 on his field goal attempts, including a blast from 57 yards for a new career-long that would have been good from 60-plus. Rookie punter Ryan Eckley averaged only 46.7 on his three punts, but all three were beauties that landed inside the 20. He didn’t make any major mistakes, which is a major compliment for the rookie. The Ravens also had good punt and kickoff returns. The Bad Pass protection: While the offensive line was dominant in the run game, they were less consistent in pass protection. There were moments that Lamar Jackson had all day to throw in a clean pocket. There were also moments where Jackson was immediately pressured into a Houdini escape act. Pro Football Focus charted the Ravens with allowing 10 pressures on 33 pass plays, and none of the starters on the line got above a 70.0 pass blocking grade. I am willing to give them some grace with a number of the starters not playing in the preseason, plus Vega Ioane and Jovaughn Gwyn getting their first NFL start against a talent like DeForest Buckner. But they need to improve, and fast. Pass game without Flowers: The Ravens started hot, hunting explosives early and often like they told us they would all offseason. But the pass game got dicey once Flowers went down. He accounted for 150 of Jackson’s 229 first-half passing yards; in the second half, Jackson did not eclipse 100. While some of that can be attributed to the Ravens going run-heavy with the lead, Flowers’ absence was clearly felt. They didn’t have much going through the air until Chris Moore caught a 53-yard deep catch-and-run late in the fourth to seal the game for Baltimore. With Flowers day-to-day and Ja’Kobi Lane down for weeks, guys like Rashod Bateman, Tez Walker, and Elijah Sarratt are going to become the focus of this wide receiver room. They will need to step up. The Ugly Penalties: This made this game closer than it ever should have been. The Ravens went into double-digit territory, totaling 10 penalties for 86 yards. Beyond the sheer amount of penalties the Ravens had, they had multiple penalties that eliminated big plays. Ja’Kobi Lane had his first career touchdown taken away by a hold. Rashod Bateman converted a first down on third and medium on a long catch that was taken away by a hold. Chris Moore had a 49-yard return that turned field position at midfield into starting inside the 20. There’s a chance the Ravens win by 30+ with ease if they don’t commit even half the penalties.

title: Buffalo Bills fans weigh in about the direction of the team entering Week 2
summary: Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bills fans and fans across the country. author: Matt Byham

title: 5 Buffalo Bills to watch vs. the Detroit Lions
summary: Fresh off a thrilling 36-31 victory over the Houston Texans, the Buffalo Bills have little time to prepare for their 2026 home opener against the Detroit Lions. A Thursday night kickoff means that the Bills have but three off days before taking the field to begin play in Week Two. Fortunately, the Bills escaped Houston […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 13: Offensive tackle Dion Dawkins #73 of the Buffalo Bills readies to block during the NFL game between the Houston Texans and the Buffalo Bills on September 13, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX.(Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Fresh off a thrilling 36-31 victory over the Houston Texans, the Buffalo Bills have little time to prepare for their 2026 home opener against the Detroit Lions. A Thursday night kickoff means that the Bills have but three off days before taking the field to begin play in Week Two. Fortunately, the Bills escaped Houston relatively healthy, which means that they’ll have nearly their full array of players available for what should be a great game. The Bills were outstanding on offense last week, putting up 36 points on a Houston defense widely regarded as one of the best units in the league. Buffalo’s own stop unit, however, left plenty of room for improvement, and while they performed better as the game progressed, they still allowed nearly 400 yards of total offense, 26 first downs, and 36 minutes of possession. With that in mind, we have a slight slant towards the defensive side of the ball for this week’s five players to watch. _____________________________________________________________________________ RB James Cook III Buffalo’s lead running back was the NFL’s leading rusher last year, and while he was efficient against a tough Texans run defense (13 carries, 57 yards), I’m looking for more out of him this week. Cook was active in the pass game, as he saw four targets to slot in behind DJ Moore, Dalton Kincaid, and Khalil Shakir in the pecking order. He caught three of those passes for just twelve yards. Cook dropped a pass late in the game when he heard the footsteps of linebacker Aziz Al’Shaiir coming. He also narrowly averted disaster when he fumbled on the opening play of what would become Buffalo’s game-winning touchdown drive. Cook had a career-high six fumbles last year in the regular season, and the fumble he lost in Buffalo’s playoff loss to the Denver Broncos swung early momentum away from the Bills and back towards the home team while Buffalo was driving. Cook doesn’t have to put up superstar numbers every week, but watching him keep hold of the ball while scoring would be a nice way to kick off Week Two and his first game at the new Highmark Stadium. LT Dion Dawkins I’ll preface this with the positive: Buffalo’s offense line did a great job against the Texans last week, as they kept Josh Allen upright and gave him time to make multiple big plays down the field. The assignment isn’t any easier this week, though, as someone is going to have to deal with Aiden Hutchinson, Detroit’s Pro Bowl pass rusher who was named Second-Team All Pro last year. If Pro Football Focus grades are your thing, Dawkins graded out as one of the five worst offensive players for the Bills last week, earning a 53.1 grade from the analytics site. Given that most of us have had high praise for Buffalo’s offensive line last week, it is a red flag for me that three of the team’s five lowest graded players on offense were linemen, as O’Cyrus Torrence (45.4) and Alec Anderson (52.4) were also in that bottom group. Dawkins had some bad reps—a whiff on corner Kamari Lassiter on Buffalo’s failed fourth-down try during the first offensive possession of the game comes to mind—but the good reps outweighed the bad. He’ll need to put together another strong performance this week against a Lions pass rush unit that sacked New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough five times last week. OLB Bradley Chubb Chubb played a ton of snaps last week, logging 63 of the team’s 79 defensive snaps. He totaled four tackles and two quarterback hits on the afternoon, which isn’t a terrible showing, but it’s not quite what we’d like to see from the veteran pass rusher. Given how disruptive Greg Rousseau was on Sunday, I assume that the Lions will look to slide protection his way. That should leave Chubb in some one-on-one situations, and it he can beat his man to pressure Jared Goff, then the Bills will be in great shape. The problem is that the Lions have an all-world left tackle in Penei Sewell. so if that’s the one v. one matchup, it’s definitely advantage Lions whether Chubb or Rousseau is across from him. Using some games and stunts up front to free up rushers is going to be the move, and new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard did a nice job generating pressure using that method with just his front four on Sunday. Look for Chubb to move around the formation a bit more this week rather than anchoring an OLB spot like he did on Sunday. CB Christian Benford Buffalo’s top corner had a tough matchup on Sunday against Nico Collins, and it was not his finest hour as a result. Collins caught seven passes for 75 yards and a score on ten targets, most of which came when matched up against Benford. Quarterback C.J. Stroud targeted Benford a whopping 11 times in the game, completing seven of those passes for a total of 75 yards and a touchdown. Benford started slowly last season, too, before turning it on late, but his matchup isn’t going to be any easier this week. Given that he traveled with Collins against the Texans, it wouldn’t surprise me to see him travel with Detroit’s top wideout, Amon-Ra St. Brown. Granted, St. Brown does more work in the slot than Collins does, so that might pose a problem or change the calculus a bit, but the Bills believe—rightly—that Benford is their best cover guy. He’s going to have to step up and try to bottle another big-play receiver this week. CB Dee Alford Two corners make the list this week, as the defensive secondary was not an area I was impressed with on Sunday. Alford, in particular, left a lot to be desired, as he seemed to miscommunicate on multiple assignments. He didn’t look great in run support, either, often coming in a step late or a step wide to expose running lanes for David Montgomery and Woody Marks. Alford has big shoes to fill given the hard-nosed example of what a nickel corner can do that Taron Johnson set over the last eight seasons, and for the first week, he did not fill them well. Detroit has a bevy of receiving options that can line up all over the formation, so Alford could see work against Amon-Ra St. Brown, tight end Sam LaPorta, or anyone in between. He’ll need to step up this week.
author: Sean Murphy

title: Buffalo Bills vs. Detroit Lions: Series history, Josh Allen record
summary: The Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions have both been around for a long time. A really long time. Yet, somehow, Thursday night will be just the 14th regular-season meeting between the two franchises.  And, because apparently 13 games spread across more than five decades isn’t weird enough, there’s this: The Bills have scored 274 points in those games. The Lions have scored 273. One point […]
full_text: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 15: James Cook #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the ball while being chased by Jamal Adams #25 of the Detroit Lions in the third quarter at Ford Field on December 15, 2024 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Mike Mulholland/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills and Detroit Lions have both been around for a long time. A really long time. Yet, somehow, Thursday night will be just the 14th regular-season meeting between the two franchises. And, because apparently 13 games spread across more than five decades isn’t weird enough, there’s this: The Bills have scored 274 points in those games. The Lions have scored 273. One point separates two teams that have been playing football for over a combined hundred years. This week’s Time Capsule takes us through a series that hasn’t given us a lot of games but has certainly given us a few worth remembering. _____________________________________________________________________________ The last time: Dec. 15, 2024 This one was supposed to be a potential Super Bowl preview. The Lions entered the afternoon 12-1 and riding an 11-game winning streak. The Bills were 10-3 and coming off a 44-42 loss to the Los Angeles Rams. Apparently, Buffalo decided 42 points wasn’t enough. The Bills walked into Ford Field and scored 48. Josh Allen threw for 362 yards and two touchdowns while adding another 68 yards and two scores on the ground. James Cook rushed for 105 yards and two touchdowns as Buffalo piled up 559 yards of offense. And they needed almost all of it. Buffalo jumped out to a 14-0 lead and stretched that advantage to 35-14 in the third quarter, but Jared Goff and the Lions weren’t going quietly. Goff threw for 494 yards and five touchdowns. Detroit scored 21 points in the fourth quarter, and a game Buffalo had seemingly put away turned into one where nobody could really relax until the clock finally hit zero. Bills 48. Lions 42. Potential Super Bowl preview? Well, we know how that part turned out. But Buffalo did leave Detroit with one of its biggest wins of the regular season, and Allen left with another addition to the increasingly ridiculous collection of games on his MVP résumé. _____________________________________________________________________________ Before that: Thanksgiving in Detroit Two years earlier, Allen and the Bills were also in Detroit. Actually, they were there for the second time in five days. A massive snowstorm in Western New York had forced Buffalo’s Week 11 game against the Cleveland Browns to Ford Field. The Bills won that one, flew home, and then turned around and went right back to Detroit for Thanksgiving. Because why make anything easy? This time, the Lions made sure Buffalo had to work until the very end. Detroit tied the game at 25 with just 23 seconds left. Allen hit Stefon Diggs for 36 yards on the first play of the ensuing drive, Buffalo moved into field-goal range, and Tyler Bass connected from 45 yards with two seconds left to give the Bills a 28-25 win. Allen finished with 253 passing yards and two touchdowns while adding 78 yards and another score on the ground. It wasn’t quite the offensive explosion we would see two years later, but the result was the same. _____________________________________________________________________________ The first one: Rookie Josh To find Allen’s first game against Detroit, we have to go all the way back to 2018. Buffalo was 4-9. Detroit was 5-8. Allen was a rookie, and the Bills were still trying to figure out exactly what they had in their first-round quarterback. There were clues. Allen threw for 204 yards and a touchdown and rushed for another score as Buffalo beat Detroit 14-13. It wasn’t 48-42, and it wasn’t a last-second Thanksgiving win, but it started a streak. Allen is now 3-0 against Detroit. Thursday night gives him a chance to make it four. _____________________________________________________________________________ How far back do we have to go? Want to find the last time the Lions beat the Bills? We need to open a slightly older Time Capsule. Oct. 15, 2006. Dick Jauron was Buffalo’s head coach. J.P. Losman was the quarterback. Willis McGahee was carrying the football. For Detroit, it was Jon Kitna at quarterback, Kevin Jones at running back, and Roy Williams catching passes. The Lions won 20-17, and they haven’t beaten Buffalo since. The Bills have won five straight meetings — in 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022, and 2024. Of course, there’s a pretty important qualifier here. Buffalo and Detroit only see each other once every four years under the NFL’s normal scheduling rotation, so a 20-year drought doesn’t exactly mean the Bills have spent two decades tormenting the Lions. But 20 years is 20 years. _____________________________________________________________________________ One stadium closes, another one opens There’s one more piece of history that makes this week’s matchup a little different. Allen’s first game against Detroit, that 14-13 win in 2018, was the last time the Lions played a regular-season game in Orchard Park. It was also their last game in the old Highmark Stadium. Now they’re back, and this time they’re part of something much bigger than the series history. Thursday night’s game will be the first regular-season game played in the new Highmark Stadium. The Bills and Lions have met only 13 times. Buffalo holds an 8-4-1 advantage. One point separates them on the all-time scoreboard. Detroit hasn’t beaten Buffalo since 2006, and Josh Allen has never lost to the Lions. But none of that history happened here. The new stadium doesn’t have a Bills-Lions story yet. Thursday night gets to write the first one.
