title: Former Eagles players Week 1 recap
summary: The Eagles are 1-0 heading into the second week of the season, but let’s take a moment to recap what some former Eagles did around the league in their season openers. It was a big day for guys like Carson Wentz and D’Andre Swift, and we got reminded that guys like Nakobe Dean and Za’Darius […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - AUGUST 27: Nakobe Dean #17 of the Las Vegas Raiders is introduced before a preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers at Allegiant Stadium on August 27, 2026 in Las Vegas, Nevada. The 49ers defeated the Raiders 18-12. (Photo by Ethan Miller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles are 1-0 heading into the second week of the season, but let’s take a moment to recap what some former Eagles did around the league in their season openers. It was a big day for guys like Carson Wentz and D’Andre Swift, and we got reminded that guys like Nakobe Dean and Za’Darius Smith are still really good. The season kicked off on a Wednesday, which means some news feels like forever ago, but one of the more notable moments from this week was A.J. Brown leaving the Patriots-Seahawks game early and ultimately landing on IR . Here are some other highlights from Philly alumni in Week 1: Carson Wentz steps up in Minnesota Heading into the Vikings season opener, Carson Wentz was named the backup to Kyler Murray. The former Eagles QB was called up even sooner than expected after Murray went down with a head injury in the first quarter. Wentz struggled at first as he got acclimated, but ended up finishing the day 12-of-19 for 133 yards and three touchdowns, bringing the Vikings back from behind to beat the Packers. Carson Wentz is the first reserve to throw 3 pass TD and 0 INT in a season-opening win since Fran Tarkenton on Sept. 17, 1961 🏈 That just so happened to be the first game in Vikings history and Tarkenton's first career game 🤯 pic.twitter.com/Wg5EBhbM1d — ESPN Insights (@ESPNInsights) September 14, 2026 D’Andre Swift signs new contract The former Eagles running back took the next step with the Bears, and they rewarded him with a new 3-year, $33.75 million contract, that included $27.5 million guaranteed. Swift went on to thank the Bears with a Week 1 performance that included 18 carries for 124 yards and three touchdowns. D'Andre Swift showing why he got that extension ‼️ CHIvsCAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/AiqMSBsMEJ — NFL (@NFL) September 13, 2026 Josh Jobe seals win The former Eagles CB grabbed the game-winning interception for the Seahawks over the Patriots in the NFL season opener, stepping in front of another Philly alumni, Mack Hollins, to make the play. Drake Maye is picked off for the 3rd time tonight, this time to Josh Jobe. #Seahawks win the opener. pic.twitter.com/hX8i7gIxXd https://t.co/gWuBWDkgBA — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 10, 2026 Nakobe Dean is still good One of the bigger losses for the Eagles this offseason was linebacker Nakobe Dean, who is already making a name for himself with the Raiders. In his first game of the season, Dean recorded six total tackles, one sack, and one forced fumble. Nakobe Dean gets to Malik Willis for the sack, and the sparkly cleat comes off again! ✨ 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/BKgJKX1Ep7 — FOX Sports: NFL (@NFLonFOX) September 13, 2026 This is an insane super man punch by Nakobe Dean but the fumble went out of bounds pic.twitter.com/DglvlB3ERJ — Ted Nguyen (@FB_FilmAnalysis) September 15, 2026 Za’Darius Smith can still play Smith retired from the NFL and the Eagles early in the 2025 season, but recently revealed the personal grief and reasonings behind that decision. Now, following a year filled with loss, he is playing for his family’s favorite team, and was dominant in his return to the field, this time for the Falcons. Zadarius Smith in his Falcons debut: – 2 sacks – 2 QB hits – 3 tackles for losses #DirtyBirds pic.twitter.com/DuoqV6gk5o — 𝙁𝙖𝙡𝙘𝙤𝙣𝙨 𝙈𝙪𝙨𝙚 (@ATLFalconsMuse) September 13, 2026 Other notables Former Eagles inactive Week 1: WR John Metchie (Panthers), OL Myles Hinton (Bengals) RB Kenny Gainwell had five carries for 15 yards and one kick return for 22 yards in the Bucs loss to the Bengals on Sunday. Several former Eagles defenders notched more than seven tackles in Week 1, including: S C.J. Gardner-Johnson – 8 (Bills), S Reed Blankenship – 7 (Texans), CB Avonte Maddox – 7 (Lions), and S Sydney Brown – 7 (Falcons). CB Tremon Smith is still doing his thing as a returner for the Houston Texans, and had two kick returns for 54 yards against the Bills. FB Ben VanSumeren was activated from the practice squad for the Chiefs Monday night game against the Broncos. The Falcons put a lot of faith in former Eagles WR Olamide Zaccheous , who due to injuries, was listed as both the emergency QB and emergency RB against the Steelers. It didn’t come to that, and Zaccheous finished the game with just one catch for five yards. Other Philly alumni for Atlanta included WR Jahan Dotson , one catch for 19 yards, and DT Kentavious Street , two tackles and one sack. Carolina played well above expectations and kept up with Chicago for awhile, before the Bears ran away with the game. QB Kenny Pickett did get a couple plays on Sunday, including one 24-yard breakaway run. Other former Eagles for the Panthers, include RB A.J. Dillon , who had five carries for 28 yards, and LB Jaelan Phillips had three total tackles and one sack.

title: Eagles News: Landon Dickerson replacement options
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! With Landon Dickerson expected to go on injured reserve, the Eagles need a new starting left guard. Drew Kendall should and likely will be be the first man up. I know people love Willie Lampkin — and I’m one of them! […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Drew Kendall #66 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on during the national anthem prior to an NFL preseason football game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! With Landon Dickerson expected to go on injured reserve, the Eagles need a new starting left guard. Drew Kendall should and likely will be be the first man up. I know people love Willie Lampkin — and I’m one of them! — but he wasn’t taking first-team reps this summer. It was Kendall filling in at LG whenever Dickerson missed time. Kendall lacks a ton of experience at guard; he only played center in college. But he’s been learning the position since entering the NFL last year. I don’t like the idea of moving Cam Jurgens to left guard and changing two starting spots on the offensive line. How do you think the team should handle this situation? Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Eagles to place guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, will miss at least four games – Inquirer Second-year offensive lineman Drew Kendall is expected to replace Dickerson, unless the Eagles decide on another configuration that could shift center Cam Jurgens to guard. Willie Lampkin is also in play for either job, although Kendall is the likely first interior lineman up. Kendall played center exclusively in college, while Jurgens’ first season as a starter in the NFL was at right guard. Jurgens also struggled against Washington on Sunday. Like Dickerson, he played through injury during the Super Bowl LIX run in 2025 and returned the following season following back surgery. He never looked 100%. Dickerson’s career, dating back to college, has been injury-plagued. He had multiple ACL tears, ankle surgeries, and other ailments during his time at Florida State and Alabama. The Eagles drafted him in the second round despite the medical red flags. He quickly became one of the NFL’s best interior linemen, though, and earned three straight Pro Bowl nods from 2022-24. But the injuries mounted, and while Dickerson missed only a handful of games in his first five seasons, it increasingly affected his performance. The Eagles’ changes to their offensive scheme this offseason were expected to affect Dickerson the most out of the starting five O-linemen. The wide-zone blocking requires more athletic and agile blockers. Eagles place Landon Dickerson on injured reserve, three thoughts on the move – PHLY Eagles I’d expect Drew Kendall to get the nod to start in Dickerson’s place this Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. Eagles general manager Howie Roseman offered a now-telling admission during a news conference last month closing out training camp that, if he’d been given truth serum going into the summer, he’d have said the interior offensive line depth was the thing he was most worried about. Kendall, along with training camp darling Willie Lampkin and sixth-round rookie Micah Morris, each had strong enough camps to quiet that worry for Roseman and Kendall seems the most ready to jump up the depth chart. “If any of you would’ve given me a truth serum and said, ‘What are you looking for in training camp?’ It would be how our interior offensive line depth panned out,” Roseman said. “Those young guys and the growth that they showed, their ability to play in the passing game, in the run game. I mean, really, really excited about those guys, about being able to have those guys, being able to develop those guys, but at the same time, have confidence that if those guys need to play, that they’re ready to play.” How will Eagles replace Landon Dickerson during his IR stint? – NBCSP Drew Kendall to center. Perhaps the loss of Dickerson will make the Eagles shuffle their line. Because Kendall is a more natural center, the Eagles could elect to plug him there and move Cam Jurgens to guard. Jurgens is a two-time Pro Bowl center but was a full-time starter at guard during the 2023 season. Former offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland normally tried to avoid shuffling the line like this because he thought it weakened them at two spots. But Stoutland isn’t their OL coach anymore and Chris Kuper might have different feelings on how to go about finding their best starting five. Landon Dickerson Update – Iggles Blitz This means Drew Kendall becomes the LG. Willie Lampkin is now the top backup interior OL. Jake Majors or John Ojukwu could be promoted from the practice squad for depth. Ojukwu has more experience. Both guys are good scheme fits. Rookie Micah Morris is talented, but I think he’s more of a long term solution than someone they would play right away. Howie Roseman talked this summer about how his big concern in the offseason was interior OL depth. The Eagles had several guys step up and perform well. Now comes the real test. I’m happy that Dickerson and the team took decisive action. If you know he’s not healthy, get him out of there. Give Kendall a chance to show what he can do. Is this the end of Dickerson’s career? It very well could be. Hopefully some time off will help him to heal and he can get back on the field one more time. No one wants to go out on a bad game. Landon Dickerson injury: Eagles guard headed to IR, admits he “was a complete liability” in Week 1 – BGN There were a lot of things to address coming out of the Philadelphia Eagles Week 1 win over the Washington Commanders, but arguably the biggest concern was starting left guard Landon Dickerson. Just one day later, the three-time Pro Bowler is expected to be heading to injured reserve, which means he will miss at least the next four games. NFC East Mixtape Vol. 189: Giants beat Cowboys, Eagles beat Washington – NFC East Mixtape The first week of the NFL season is just about over, and wow do we have some NFC East action to discuss! To start… the New York Giants actually did it. They announced that maybe this time finally is different as they completely dismantled the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday night. Earlier in the day, the Philadelphia Eagles withstood a rally from the Washington Commanders for more of the same as far as recent history is concerned. How are we feeling about all four teams as we move on into the actual season? RJ Ochoa and Brandon Lee Gowton discuss! You can see that we have a BRAND NEW NFC East Mixtape YouTube Channel so make sure to subscribe as the show will live here exclusively in video format. AND you can also listen to the show! On Blogging The Boys and/or Bleeding Green Nation podcast feeds as well as the SB Nation NFL Show feed! NFC Hierarchy/Obituary: Week 2 edition – PhillyVoice 5) Eagles (1-0): The Eagles’ defense kept the Commanders from doing much of anything until the fourth quarter, and Jalen Hurts made enough plays to win the Eagles the game, but 10 first downs was the second-fewest in the NFL Week 1, behind only the Broncos. The Titans had 11. The Dolphins had 13. Even the Browns had 15. And the Eagles played against one of the worst defenses in the NFL. Not good enough. Last week: 3. The Philadelphia Eagles changed offensive coordinators. Their second-half problem remains – The Athletic There were new schemes, new coaches, but ultimately a continuation of a year-old problem. Jalen Hurts’ second-half heroics allow new Philadelphia Eagles offensive coordinator Sean Mannion to solve second-half stalls in the safety of the win column — much like his predecessor did until the stalls eventually did him in. The 2025 Eagles were the only team in coach Nick Sirianni’s tenure to finish a season with a negative second-half scoring margin (-7). The 2026 Eagles own a minus-3 second-half point differential after Week 1. Debuts offer some forgiveness. So do wins. Mannion, a first-time play caller, will look back on a mostly brutal 20-play sequence that portrayed the antithesis of the “aggressive”…

title: T.J. Watt already buying into playing fewer snaps
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers kicked off the 2026 season with a 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons, marking their third consecutive Week 1 win, and their sixth opening win over the last seven seasons. The Steelers largely won off the strength of a vintage performance from T.J. Watt. The star edge rusher looked like his old […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: T.J. Watt #90 of the Pittsburgh Steelers warms up prior to the game against the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers kicked off the 2026 season with a 20-13 win over the Atlanta Falcons, marking their third consecutive Week 1 win, and their sixth opening win over the last seven seasons. The Steelers largely won off the strength of a vintage performance from T.J. Watt. The star edge rusher looked like his old self, racking up two sacks, three tackles for loss, and his first career pick-six that iced the win for Pittsburgh. One of the more noteworthy developments from the game, though, was the intentional lower snap count for Watt and all three of the top edge rushers for Pittsburgh. Watt played just 38 snaps, which accounted for 63 percent of defensive snaps. For reference, he hasn’t played in lower than 82 percent of the snaps in games he’s played since 2021. Appearing on Cam Heyward’s Not Just Football podcast, Watt says he feels great and credited a lower snap count for it, “My body feels significantly better,” Watt said. “I feel way better. And you know how it is, you want to be out there every play. You feel like any play you’re not out there is a missed opportunity to make a play. Especially guys that can make splash [plays] like you can.” Watt credits linebackers coach C.J. Ah You for managing the reps of the edge rushers. “I think that’s something I didn’t really recognize was in C.J.‘s repertoire was managing reps like that,” Watt said. “I think that’s a skill, honestly, to be able to rotate us. Especially, as you know, with me, Herb, Jack, and Alex, sometimes there’s three of us out there on the field at the same time… I think that’s a skill that C.J. put on display on Sunday.” Watt and the Steelers will head to New England in Week 2 to take on the Patriots – a game they won a season ago 21-14. title: Steelers try out former Texans offensive lineman
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers are exploring another option along their offensive line, bringing in veteran offensive tackle Charlie Heck for a tryout Tuesday. According to Steelers insider Alan Saunders, the Steelers tried out Heck, a former fourth-round pick of the Houston Texans out of North Carolina. Heck, 28, spent the 2026 preseason with the Miami Dolphins […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - DECEMBER 18: Charlie Heck #67 of the Houston Texans get set against the Kansas City Chiefs at NRG Stadium on December 18, 2022 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers are exploring another option along their offensive line, bringing in veteran offensive tackle Charlie Heck for a tryout Tuesday. According to Steelers insider Alan Saunders , the Steelers tried out Heck, a former fourth-round pick of the Houston Texans out of North Carolina. Heck, 28, spent the 2026 preseason with the Miami Dolphins before becoming available on the open market. He originally entered the NFL as a fourth-round selection by Houston in the 2020 NFL Draft. The 6-foot-8, 310-pound tackle has appeared in 51 regular-season games during his NFL career, including 27 starts. His experience comes primarily at offensive tackle, giving Pittsburgh another veteran option as it continues to evaluate the depth of its offensive line. The Steelers also hosted tackle Austin Deculus, a 2022 sixth-round pick by Houston, for a tryout, according to KPRC2’s Aaron Wilson . Deculus has six career starts and has appeared in 26 career games. The Steelers have already made significant changes up front this offseason, with new head coach Mike McCarthy installing a different offensive system. Pittsburgh’s transition from Arthur Smith’s wide-zone approach to McCarthy’s more traditional pro-style, gap-oriented scheme has placed additional emphasis on finding players who fit the new system. Heck and Deculus’ workouts do not necessarily mean the Steelers will sign them, but it signals that the team is continuing to examine available veteran options at tackle.

title: Steelers Week 2 power rankings roundup: Any love for Pittsburgh after beating Cooper Rush?
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers started the Mike McCarthy era on a high note by defeating the Atlanta Falcons at home Sunday afternoon, 20-13. After a shaky start, it was the Steelers’ defense that stole the show and propelled the team to victory. That included a pick-six from TJ Watt, who looked fresh and revitalized under this […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 13: Pat Freiermuth #88 of the Pittsburgh Steelers celebrates with teammates after scoring a touchdown against the Atlanta Falcons during the second quarter of the game at Acrisure Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers started the Mike McCarthy era on a high note by defeating the Atlanta Falcons at home Sunday afternoon, 20-13. After a shaky start, it was the Steelers’ defense that stole the show and propelled the team to victory. That included a pick-six from TJ Watt, who looked fresh and revitalized under this new coaching staff. It’s time for our weekly look around the web to see where the Steelers fall in this week’s power rankings. FOX Sports: No. 16 (No. 20 Last Week) “Aaron Rodgers was OK, not great, but he didn’t need to do a lot thanks to a defense that was stifling against a battered Falcons team playing its third-string QB.” – Ralph Vacchiano The Athletic: No. 16 (Last Week No.18) “Yes, the Steelers have a new coach, but this team looked much like it has in recent years. The defense was pretty good. The offense was mostly fine. It’s rarely worth putting too much stock into Week 1, but this Mike McCarthy-led squad looks like another roughly .500 team. We should learn more about the Steelers in Week 2 during their trip to New England.” – Chad Graff and Josh Kendall CBS Sports: No.20 (Last Week No. 20) “They beat the Falcons, but it wasn’t pretty. They have to do more on offense, starting this week against the Patriots.” – Pete Prisco Pro Football Talk: No. 17 (Last Week No. 18) “For the second time in three years, T.J. Watt personally delivered a win over the Falcons in Week 1.” – Mike Florio NFL.com: No. 23 (Last Week No.21) “Mike McCarthy’s debut as Steelers coach didn’t come with the explosive offense that was his trademark at prior NFL stops. Aaron Rodgers played with more freedom and aggression than he did last season, but the unit struggled to produce points against the Falcons. None of that matters all that much, though, when T.J. Watt is intercepting passes and turning them into defensive touchdowns.” – Nick Shook Yahoo! Sports: No. 20 (Last Week No. 20) “The Steelers got a win but it wasn’t pretty. Facing a Falcons team down to its third quarterback, the Steelers led by just three points in the fourth quarter before T.J. Watt had an interception return for a touchdown. Particularly troubling was the offense, which had the worst success rate in the NFL for Week 1. The run game really struggled, with 2.8 yards per carry. And that’s against a Falcons defense that wasn’t projected to be very good.“ – Frank Schwab USA Today: No. 20 (Last Week No.21) “OLB T.J. Watt appeared revived Sunday after a subpar 2025 season. He (and Joey Porter?) also looked like a player who might be a tremendous target at this season’s trade deadline.” – Nate Davis ESPN: No. 21 (Last Week No. 21) “Even with Falcons do-everything back Bijan Robinson racking up 173 scrimmage yards, it’s hard to point to anyone other than Graham. The Steelers’ pass rush dominated third-string quarterback Cooper Rush, and the buy-in from the Steelers’ veterans was evident. T.J. Watt, who admitted he was stubborn about the idea of moving around in the old scheme, did just that Sunday. Not only did Watt have a pick-six, but he also recorded a sack from each side of the D-line. Graham passed his first test with flying colors.” – Brooke Pryor While a few publications gave the Steelers slight bumps after their Week 1 victory, most kept the Steelers exactly where they had them before the season. Given the overall lack of offensive juice the team showed, coupled with the fact that they faced a third-string quarterback, it’s hard to be upset with that way of thinking. We should learn more about the Steelers after their date with the New England Patriots in Foxborough this weekend. Let us know what you think in the comments . title: With Sam Darnold out, who could the Seahawks look to sign as a third quarterback?
summary: With Sam Darnold dealing with a glute injury that will likely sideline him for the “short-term”, the Seattle Seahawks may not need to go looking for other starting quarterback options. However, there have been reports that Darnold may be out a little longer. One report from Mike Florio even mentioned that Darnold could be out […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - NOVEMBER 17: Jake Browning #3 of the Washington Huskies runs with the ball in the first quarter against the Oregon State Beavers during their game at Husky Stadium on November 17, 2018 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Abbie Parr/Getty Images) | Getty Images With Sam Darnold dealing with a glute injury that will likely sideline him for the “short-term” , the Seattle Seahawks may not need to go looking for other starting quarterback options. However, there have been reports that Darnold may be out a little longer. One report from Mike Florio even mentioned that Darnold could be out 4-6 weeks . Regardless of the timeline, Seattle looks to only have two healthy quarterbacks for the time being. That raises the question of whether the Seahawks should look for other quarterback options, not necessarily to start – Drew Lock is likely your best bet there – but rather to add depth to the room. Counting the practice squad, John Schneider has often had three quarterbacks in the room. The third quarterback was usually your practice squad type (Alex McGough, Brett Rypien, Jaren Hall, Holton Ahlers, Sean Mannion, John Rhys Plumlee). More recently the third quarterback, Jalen Milroe, has had to be rostered due to the likelihood of him being plucked off waivers if waived. Now, with Darnold’s injury, could Schneider look to add another quarterback for temporary depth to the room? Perhaps another quarterback could come in and be Drew Lock’s primary backup, in case the Seahawks are not comfortable with Milroe being one snap away from taking legitimate NFL quarterbacks snaps in a game. With that, let’s take a look at a few options the Seahawks could look at for the quarterback position. Jake Retzlaff This first name may not look familiar to many fans, unless you were watching lots of AAC college football over the years. Retzlaff, an undrafted rookie out of Tulane was the biggest quarterback name that was at the Seahawks 2026 Rookie Minicamp . The tryout did not end up in a contract for Retzlaff. However, Seattle often will keep their eyes on the tryout players before bringing them back later in the season if injuries or other circumstances necessitate it. In his final college season at Tulane, Retzlaff completed 61% of his passes his final year at Tulane, throwing for 3,168 yards, 15 touchdowns and 7 interceptions . However, Retzlaff is also a dual threat quarterback, rushing for 634 yards and 16 touchdowns that final season alone. Retzlaff could potentially be a third quarterback option behind Milroe if Seattle feels the need to have another quarterback in the room. Josh Johnson The complete opposite of an undrafted rookie free agent, is Josh Johnson. Johnson is a 19-year NFL veteran quarterback who has played for seemingly half of the NFL, played in the United Football League, the XFL, and was even the first overall pick in the now defunct Alliance of American Football League . One team he has not played for however – the Seahawks. Adding Johnson would be like adding another coach to the quarterback room. Johnson throughout his career has been a backup or third string quarterback who only went into games in emergency situations – remember the 2022 NFC Championship game where Brock Purdy got hurt? Johnson was the quarterback who played in relief of Purdy . More recently Johnson started two games for the Washington Commanders in 2025. In those two games, he completed 63% of his passes, throwing for 372 yards, one touchdown, and two interceptions . Johnson is currently on the Cincinnati Bengals practice squad. Meaning the Seahawks would have to sign him to the 53-man roster to get him to the team. The Seahawks making a move like this would be a sign that Darnold’s injury may be longer term than originally thought. However, Johnson would not be a bad veteran option to help backup Lock and potentially Milroe as well. An added fun fact – Johnson is first cousins, and close childhood friends with Marshawn Lynch . Jake Browning A more familiar name to those in the Pacific Northwest is former Washington Huskies quarterback, Jake Browning. Browning signed with the Minnesota Vikings as an undrafted free agent in 2019. His first real game action did not come until 2023 with the Bengals. Browning started seven games that season in place of injured Joe Burrow, going 4-3 during that time. Browning impressed in his limited time. He completed 70.4% of his passes, throwing for 1,936 yards, 12 touchdowns and 7 interceptions . However, since then Browning has not been able to replicate the 2023 season. Last season when Burrow got hurt again, Browning struggled mightily. This led to the Bengals trading for Joe Flacco, positioning Browning on the outs with the organization. Browning signed with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers this offseason, however did not make the roster and is currently a free agent. The Seahawks could look to bring Browning back to the pacific northwest on the practice squad. Despite a lackluster last few years, Browning has real game experience and could be a backup option to Lock if the team is not comfortable with Milroe starting just yet. Brandon Allen One last free agent that could be an option is Brandon Allen, another longtime backup quarterback. However, Allen has one thing the other options above do not. He has worked with Seahawks offensive coordinator Brian Fleury in the past. Along with his many NFL stops, Allen was with the San Francisco 49ers in 2023 and 2024. Although Fleury was the tight ends coach with the 49ers at this time, the two surely are familiar with each other more so than others on this list. Allen is currently in his eleventh season in the NFL, but has only started ten games during that time. His most recent start came in 2024 with Fleury and the 49ers. In that game, Allen completed 56.7% of his passes, throwing for 199 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions . More recently, Allen spent 2025 with the Tennessee Titans before signing with the New York Giants this offseason. Allen was cut by the Giants during final roster cuts and is currently free to sign with anyone. Of the options above, there clearly are not that many that create much excitement. Unless Seattle looks to trade for a backup option (Tanner McKee, Anthony Richardson, etc), these are the options the team is left with. The best news the team can have is that Darnold will be back sooner than later, and that any quarterback they need to bring in (if any) are simply for depth, and not with the goal of them playing any meaningful snaps.

title: The 5 biggest surprises from the 49ers in Week 1
summary: We asked San Francisco 49ers fans what they thought were the biggest surprises from the Week 1 mashing of the Rams. There was no shortage of answers, because there was no shortage of ways the Niners stood out, both individually and as a team. Today, we’ll highlight the biggest surprises from the Niners Week 1 […]
full_text: (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images We asked San Francisco 49ers fans what they thought were the biggest surprises from the Week 1 mashing of the Rams. There was no shortage of answers, because there was no shortage of ways the Niners stood out, both individually and as a team. Today, we’ll highlight the biggest surprises from the Niners Week 1 win, based on your responses. We narrowed them down from 50. The 49ers offensive line shines OL play. I can’t remember the last time I saw them absolutely bully a defensive line, much less one supposedly as amazing as this year’s Rams, in the way they did. — SoCal delenda est🏜🌉 (@The530Bro) September 15, 2026 Trent Williams played like a Hall of Famer. That’s where he set the bar. But overall, each player consistently won their individual matchups. As a unit, they kept the quarterback upright in pass protection and excelled on the ground. The running backs weren’t touched, on average, until 2.79 yards downfield. That was the best mark of any team in the NFL in Week 1. The offense averaged 3.17 yards needed to gain on third downs. And they only had 12 of those. Those numbers show an offensive line dominating. Raheem Morris’s coverage schemes Not so much surprised but impressed by Raheem coverage schemes. Matt looked lost — DS (@DSLION904) September 15, 2026 Morris leaned into coverage in this game, blitzing Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford only 10.3% of the time. The 49ers were middle-of-the-pack in both 1-high and 2-high coverages. They only ran man coverage 18% of the time. Re-watching the game, it felt like Stafford had a hard time distinguishing the coverage, thanks to the safeties rotating post-snap. The 49ers rotated their safeties nearly 45% of the time last Thursday, which was the fourth-highest in Week 1. Here’s a breakdown of the coverage usage, with two plays unknown: Cover 3 : 9 plays, 66.7% success rate (6 of 9) Cover 6 : 9 plays, 77.8% success rate (7 of 9) Cover 1 : 5 plays, 80.0% success rate (4 of 5) Cover 4 : 4 plays, 25.0% success rate (1 of 4) Stafford was forced to check the ball down time and time again. He had three completions on ten attempts over 10 yards, with one interception. That tells me Stafford wasn’t seeing the field well and didn’t have anywhere to throw the ball. Kaelon Black in the game early Honestly, that Coach didn't overuse CMC — Chuck Beretz (@ChuckBeretz) September 15, 2026 Arguably the biggest surprise of the game came when Kyle Shanahan used his rookie running back on the first drive of the game. Black had a carry and a reception on the first drive. And he came onto the field for the second drive. Nobody in their right minds would have predicted that Black would have more carries than Christian McCaffrey in Week 1. McCaffrey ran 18 routes compared to Black’s 10. The game script set up perfectly for Black to get snaps in the fourth quarter. You don’t need McCaffrey taking any unnecessary hits. It’s one week, but that’s the kind of rotation that’ll keep McCaffrey on the field all season. Deebo Samuel’s impact Why we haven't been using Deebo in kick returns since he was a rookie. — JayJayLockerius (@JayLockeriusII) September 14, 2026 Deebo looking svelte, in shape, and doing his thing….no drop off — Chili Dog (@HighOnLiberty) September 14, 2026 Deebo looked like Deebo, with 62.5% of his receiving yards coming after the catch. He was involved on quick throws, he lined up in the backfield, and he made himself available to Brock Purdy on a scramble drill that led to a touchdown. I thought Deebo changed the game with his kickoff return to open the third quarter. It was a chance for the Rams to take control of the game, but once the Niners got the ball around midfield, that was all she wrote. Deebo was built to return kickoffs under the new rules. My bold prediction is that he’ll finish in the top five in average among all kickoff returners this season, which is great news for the offense. Nick Bosa didn’t miss a beat For me it was how well Nick Bosa played from the first snap! I thought he might be done but he shut my mouth. He played ferocious and fast. The OLine was surprising as well. That and how fast that whole Defense looked. IMO — Madlock (@kevinlmatlock) September 15, 2026 Nick Bosa has only been practicing for a maximum of two weeks. So for him to be a dominant force in under 60% of the snaps is something that feels like it’s being taken for granted. Now, it helps that the Niners didn’t get into a shootout where they’d be on the field for 70+ snaps. Bosa played 33 snaps, but recorded four run stops that were all impact plays, and made Stafford pay the price on the first play of the game. I’d argue Bosa was the 49ers’ best defensive tackle in Week 1. A couple of Bosa’s run stops came when he reduced down to a tackle in Morris’s different fronts. That allowed a guard to block him, and Bosa isn’t going to lose that battle. Surprise, surprise, it helps to have a Defensive Player of the Year candidate back on the field.

Hodge only played four special teams snaps in Week 1, both […]
full_text: (Photo by Martin KEEP / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler tweeted that the San Francisco 49ers are promoting wide receiver KhaDarel Hodge to the active roster. That creates an open spot on the practice squad, which we’ll likely find out about later on Wednesday when Kyle Shanahan speaks to the media. Hodge only played four special teams snaps in Week 1, both on the kickoff and kickoff return units. He’s expected to play a bigger role moving forward with De’Zhaun Stribling’s injury and the domino effect it’ll have on the rest of the wide receiver corps. According to Adam Schefter, the 49ers are playing Stribling on the Injured Reserve. Stribling will miss at least four games due to an ankle injury. Shanahan might have an updated timetable for Stribling, but don’t hold your breath. This move was expected. It still feels like Stribling avoided the worst-case scenario after what looked like the dreaded non-contact injury. Let’s say Stribling misses 8 games and the ankle injury is more severe than initially anticipated. That’s a better outcome than what you were probably thinking when you saw Stribling unable to put any weight on his leg during Week 1. Here is what the wide receiver room looks like heading into Week 2: Mike Evans Demarcus Robinson Deebo Samuel Jacob Cowing Jordan Watkins KhaDarel Hodge Here’s how many routes each player ran last week: Evans – 23 Robinson -18 Samuel – 18 Stribling – 13 Cowing – 3 Hodge – 1 The 49ers officially placed Jake Tonges on the Injured Reserve with a knee injury and signed tight end Jack Stoll from the practice squad. We’ll have updates later today from Shanahan. Maybe we’ll find out how far away Christian Kirk is from returning.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers in review: We’re buying stock in the secondary
summary: As we get ready to turn the page to the Miami Dolphins, let’s take one last look at the San Francisco 49ers’ Week 1 undressing of the Los Angeles Rams. What are some things that happened in Australia that could be things to watch for as the 49ers return stateside? What players stood out? Which […]
full_text: (Photo by Morgan Hancock/Getty Images) | Getty Images As we get ready to turn the page to the Miami Dolphins, let’s take one last look at the San Francisco 49ers’ Week 1 undressing of the Los Angeles Rams. What are some things that happened in Australia that could be things to watch for as the 49ers return stateside? What players stood out? Which play was the most impressive? Let’s officially close the book on Week 1 with our first game in review of 2026: Nick Bosa: run stopper? The returns of Fred Warner and Nick Bosa were the two biggest headlines for the defense heading into Week 1. Warner lived up to his standard, exiting Week 1 as the most impressive 49er in Australia. Bosa, however, left a bit to be desired. While the 49ers pass rush created 14 pressures on 28 Rams pass attempts, there was little impact felt from the front four. Bosa was no exception, collecting just one pressure and one quarterback hit on 20 pass-rush snaps. But surprisingly, it wasn’t Bosa’s pass rush ability that was the story; it was his play against the run. While the 49ers defense as a whole struggled against the run, allowing 122 yards on 29 carries, Bosa’s performance especially stood out. Bosa led the 49ers with four run stops on 16 run-play snaps, responsible for a third of the 49ers’ run stops on his own. Bosa’s pass rush ability will come around at some point as he’s returning from the season-ending injury suffered in 2025, but if Week 1 run-stopper Bosa can show up consistently, it would only add depth to the already uber-talented defensive end. A two-player running back room Maybe what happened on Thursday night was a blip and Kaelon Black will never out-carry Christian McCaffrey again. But the fact that it’s something that happened in Week 1 makes it significant. Here’s a list of games where a 49ers running back not named Christian McCaffrey has 14 or more carries in a game where McCaffrey played: Elijah Mitchell, 18 carries – Week 10 2022 Elijah Mitchell 17 carries – Week 17 2023 Kaelon Black 14 carries – Week 1 2026 And Black was deserving of those carries. The rookie gained 65 yards on his 14 attempts, looking explosive with the ball in his hands, with his longest run of the night a 14-yard carry on the 99-yard touchdown-scoring drive. While Black impressed in his debut, McCaffrey showed why he’s still the top back in the offense. On four fewer carries, McCaffrey gained more yards than Black, with a 10-carry, 68-yard performance in the season opener. McCaffrey also added five receptions for 20 yards while Black finished with one for five yards. This is likely the most interesting thing to watch over the next few weeks. Was it a coincidence that Black out-carried McCaffrey, or was it intentional? Position Group of the Week Several position groups could have earned this spot. We just discussed the running back room. The receiving corps was just as solid. And Fred Warner’s performance alone could have given it to the linebackers. But I am going to go with the cornerback group as the inaugural position group of the week. Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are as fearsome of a duo the league has to offer, and the 49ers cornerbacks held them quiet. Deommodore Lenoir was targeted four times against Nacua, allowing 28 yards on three receptions, with the biggest blemish being a 23-yard reception allowed. Other than that, Lenoir was solid against the Rams’ top receiver. On the other side, Renardo Green handled his business. When in coverage against Adams or Nacua, Green was targeted three times, allowing two receptions to Adams for 23 yards. But the lone time Matthew Stafford targeted Nacua with Green in coverage, Green hauled in the first interception of his career. Jack Jones and Upton Stout contributed as well, with the duo targeted seven times against Nacua and Adams, allowing just two receptions for eight yards, with Jones having two near-interceptions but settling with a pair of pass breakups. Because of the corners, Stafford completed just 60 percent of his passes, which is a pretty significant percentage for the quarterback from 2025. In the four games Stafford completed 60 percent or less of his passes in 2025, the Rams went 1-3. The 49ers’ cornerback play against Stafford and his top-two targets was just as important as anything else that led to the 49ers’ 20-point win. Touchdown of the Week There are three very good choices for this category, with Brock Purdy having a trio of highlight throws going for scores. The first a beautiful deep throw to Demarcus Robinson for a 39-yard touchdown followed by a connection with Mike Evans taking advantage of a one-on-one in a goal line situation. But this week’s touchdown of the week goes to Purdy’s third and final touchdown pass: Slimebo's back in business 😤 📺 Netflix pic.twitter.com/D8bs7y89AJ — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) September 11, 2026 For multiple reasons, it earns the nod, so let’s start with Purdy. He starts with an excellent slide to the right outside of the pocket the second he feels pressure. But then there’s the throw. As he’s rolling to his right, he puts the ball perfectly over a pair of Rams defenders, perfectly leading Deebo Samuel into the open spot of the end zone for the score. And that’s the other reason this particular score earns touchdown of the week: it’s not any Deebo Samuel, but it’s No. 19, Deebo Samuel. Nostalgia is what the Robinson and Evans scores are lacking. It was the perfect exclamation point for Samuel’s return to San Francisco, closing a six-catch, 48-yard day with his first touchdown as a 49er since December 30, 2024. Oh, and it was also the dagger in a rout of the Rams.

title: 49ers considered favorites to win NFC West after Week 1
summary: Through one week, the NFC West is 3-1, with the lone loss being the Los Angeles Rams, who fell to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. While the spread was 3.5-points, not many had faith in the 49ers, myself included, after the Rams added a ton of star talent in the offseason, making them the […]
full_text: MELBOURNE, AUSTRALIA - SEPTEMBER 11: Deebo Samuel Sr. #19 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates scoring a touchdown in the fourth quarter of the NFL football game against Los Angeles Rams at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on September 11, 2026 in Melbourne, Australia. (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images Through one week, the NFC West is 3-1, with the lone loss being the Los Angeles Rams, who fell to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia. While the spread was 3.5-points, not many had faith in the 49ers, myself included, after the Rams added a ton of star talent in the offseason, making them the odds-on favorites to win the Super Bowl. With the Super Bowl-winning Seattle Seahawks still around with their nucleus of players, they were also considered above the 49ers for both the NFC West and the Super Bowl. But things have quickly shifted after Week 1, when the 49ers beat the Rams 27-7 and showed the potential of what their team can do when healthy. According to ESPN, the 49ers have jumped from third to first in NFC West odds, climbing up to +160 odds to win the division. The Seahawks are shortly behind at +175, and the Rams, who were hovering around +100 to begin the season, are now third at +205 odds. However, that hasn’t changed the big-picture outlook as much. ESPN still has the Rams as the odds-on favorites to win the Super Bowl at +650, while the 49ers are tied for the fifth-best odds with the Kansas City Chiefs at +1400. Ahead of them are the Baltimore Ravens (+900), Buffalo Bills (+950), and Seattle Seahawks (+1100). It’s interesting that oddsmakers don’t see the Rams as the NFC West division winner, but they do still have them as the favorite to win the Super Bowl. The 49ers, however, do have better odds to win the NFC than the Seahawks. Los Angeles is seen as the favorite to make the Super Bowl out of the NFC at +455, while the 49ers jump up to second with +550 odds. The Seahawks are shortly behind at +580, while the Philadelphia Eagles (+710) and Chicago Bears (+800) round out the top five. There have been some early injuries shifting the tune in the NFC West. Los Angeles will be without star pass rusher Myles Garrett for at least the next month after placing him on Injured Reserve. Of course, Aaron Donald has yet to play as well. Sam Darnold is dealing with a hip injury and will also be out, making Drew Lock the starter for the upcoming weeks. The 49ers have dealt with their mass of injuries already, with players like Ricky Pearsall and Alfred Collins set to miss the season, but their core group of stars was all healthy for Week 1. San Francisco will first face the Seahawks on the road in Week 5 after three straight home games against the Miami Dolphins, Arizona Cardinals, and Denver Broncos. That could be the next major game that shifts the division odds one way or another, and could also be around when Sam Darnold returns.
author: Rohan Chakravarthi

title: 49ers News: Welcome to the Bay, McKinnley Jackson!
summary: The Miami Dolphins are begging to be overlooked. A trap game this early sounds insane, I know, but after coming back from such a long flight and an emotional win… going against an opponent that doesn’t seem like much… let’s not forget that the Dolphins are still an NFL team. The 49ers are going against […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX-DECEMBER 9: McKinnley Jackson #93 of the Cincinnati Bengals looks on during the game at AT&T Stadium on December 9, 2024 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins are begging to be overlooked. A trap game this early sounds insane, I know, but after coming back from such a long flight and an emotional win… going against an opponent that doesn’t seem like much… let’s not forget that the Dolphins are still an NFL team. The 49ers are going against a young, hungry, mobile QB-led team with nothing to lose and everything to gain from embarrassing the 49ers. They started rallying on the Raiders before the Raiders put them away. WR Caleb Douglas seems like the real deal, so the 49ers secondary can’t be coasting just because they shut down Puka Nacua and Davante Adams. Everybody better lock in at practice today. 49ers Week 1 Tape Takeaways: Motion commotion (paywall) “The 49ers looked coordinated in the run game. They went back to their zone-heavy roots, and I wonder if leaning on Dash helped simplify things. It made things easier for the offensive line and made every run look the same (sometimes they were). San Francisco consistently attacked the Rams’ weak linebacker corps. The coordination on help blocks and second-level climbs was outstanding. Colby looked weak at times, and allowed a team-high six run stops (my measure), but he also had great moments. This is, at this moment, a legitimately good offensive line. A healthy Trent Williams and Dom Puni make a massive difference…The 49ers didn’t really go to dime looks until the fourth quarter, once the Rams had all but abandoned their run game and 13 personnel looks. I love it. Raheem Morris used the 49ers’ best DBs, letting Deommodore Lenoir thrive in that Star/Jackal/Apex/positionless position that’s really just a second nickel. We’ll see how much they lean on dime going forward, but I’d be stunned if this was a one-off experiment. It was too effective….Also, I enjoyed how effective the 49ers were at running stunts. They were far cleaner than in the past. It created a lot of effective disruption, and helped limit some of the wear and tear Nick Bosa would face with head-up rushes….Lastly, George Kittle. He doesn’t look near where he was last year before his injury and I wouldn’t expect him to. I say that while also noting that he had some nice blocks on the move. But he can’t really power off his surgically-repaired right leg.” 49ers mailbag: What’s next after De’Zhaun Stribling’s and Alfred Collins’ injuries? (Paywall) “But I still think the bigger need is at defensive end. Though Mykel Williams is technically a defensive end, he’ll be able to play a lot of defensive tackle snaps — especially on obvious passing downs — when he’s back after Week 4. The same goes for Keion White. There are also a lot more quality defensive ends available, a list that includes Haason Reddick, Leonard Floyd and Joey Bosa. Here’s how I’d classify them: If the team wants another Romello Height-like player or is worried it’s not getting enough out of Height, Reddick would be a good solution. He’s a lighter-bodied edge player who’s played in systems similar to the one defensive coordinator Raheem Morris is running this year. If the team wants a dependable, every-down defensive end, Floyd is the answer. He’s familiar to both the 49ers’ brass and Morris. Yes, Floyd turned 34 last week and had only 3.5 sacks last year for Morris’ Falcons. But the 49ers aren’t in a position to look down their noses at 3.5 sacks. Their sack leader last year had four. If the 49ers want a second-half-of-the-season boost, how about Bosa? The team might be worried about how Nick Bosa’s oft-injured older brother might hold up over a 17-game season. But an eight-game season seems reasonable. Joey had five sacks and 54 quarterback pressures for the Bills last year. That’s not elite, but it’s better than what the 49ers have opposite Nick at the moment. Another interesting option is Yetur Gross-Matos, whose recent stint with the 49ers was marred by a knee issue. Gross-Matos didn’t play or practice much, but when he was on the field, he made an impact. His 16.3 percent pass-rush win rate last season was second best on the team behind Bosa’s 20 percent rate. Gross-Matos is currently rehabilitating from that knee injury and isn’t ready to play. That could change by midseason.” Download the SB Nation app today! Will 49ers’ De’Zhaun Stribling need an ankle procedure? Surgeons explain factors at play (paywall) “To be clear, most deltoid ligament sprains heal on their own. And that could be the case with Stribling. But the nature of the injury is why athletes are sidelined for at least a month — with some recoveries requiring up to six weeks — if surgery isn’t required. Jung and Dr. Nicholas Strasser, a foot and ankle surgeon who is consultant to the Tennessee Titans and Vanderbilt University, explained that the deltoid ligament is a stronger ligament than the two on the outside of the ankle that are associated with low and high ankle sprains. As a result, it requires more force to damage the deltoid. And more force means more trauma to the ankle. …Jung said Stribling would have already had a procedure if he had “gross instability,” but it’s likely premature to say whether rest and rehabilitation will restore whatever instability Stribling is experiencing. Stribling’s stability will be determined by how the fibers in his torn ankle heal. “If they heal a little bit stretched out, or in a way that it just doesn’t have enough support to it, that could lead to surgery,” said Strasser, an assistant professor of orthopedics at Vanderbilt. “Especially because it’s on the inside part of the ankle and you’re often cutting and pushing off that a little bit more. The stress in that area is a little bit more extreme.” If Stribling needs surgery, his recovery would last three to four months, which would sideline him for most or all of the regular season.” 49ers overreactions: Will 2026 NFL season be a touchdown frenzy for Brock Purdy? “Mike Evans and George Kittle are the most-likely players to have 10 or more touchdown catches. Christian McCaffrey and Deebo Samuel are candidates to team up with Purdy for a lot of scoring receptions, too.” 49ers find needed balance in run game with McCaffrey, Black “From midfield, Brendel turned toward coach Kyle Shanahan on the sideline and waved his arms to suggest he wanted to run the ball, run it again and keep running it until the Rams showed they could at least slow it down. “After a few of those good chunk run plays hit, I’m looking right at Kyle, ‘Let’s go,'” Brendel said. “Let’s just keep going. Let’s keep dialing them up.” Shanahan apparently agreed with Brendel’s assessment. The success of those plays only yielded more runs, and by the end of San Francisco’s 27-7 win, it had 30 attempts for a robust 5.8 yards per rush….San Francisco also took advantage of a schematic curveball from the Rams. According to Brendel, the Niners spent the week preparing for plenty of five-man fronts — similar to what Los Angeles threw at them in recent matchups. Brendel was surprised when the Rams not only played four down linemen more frequently but were also often in nickel packages (five defensive backs). “The way that they chose to play us on defense schematically we weren’t really expecting,” Brendel said. “Most teams are a little bit more scared of our wide zone and our run game.” 49ers’ Renardo Green credits experience for his big interception vs. Rams “I knew the way I played it, I knew he (Stafford) didn’t see me, and even if he did, he didn’t think I could get to it,” Green told NBC Sports Bay Area. “He underestimated my abilities and what I could do, and he paid for it. I sunk under it and made a play on the ball….“Once I made it, I…

title: 49ers sign Jack Stoll to the practice squad after Jake Tonges injury
summary: The San Francisco 49ers hosted five players for a tryout after tight end Jake Tonges and defensive tackle Alfred Collins suffered injuries. The team already added a defensive tackle to the practice squad on Tuesday. Here are the three tight ends and a pair of defensive tackles the team worked out: TE Lawrence Cager (6’5”, […]
full_text: (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers hosted five players for a tryout after tight end Jake Tonges and defensive tackle Alfred Collins suffered injuries. The team already added a defensive tackle to the practice squad on Tuesday . Here are the three tight ends and a pair of defensive tackles the team worked out: TE Lawrence Cager (6’5”, 220) TE Tanner Conner (6’3”, 232) TE Jack Stoll (6’4”, 247) DT Larry Ogunjobi DT Daniel Ekuale Cager, 29, has been in the NFL since 2020, but he hasn’t played a regular-season game since 2023. He spent his NFL tenure with the Jets and the Giants. His most productive season came in 2022, when he caught 13 passes for 118 yards. Conner went undrafted in the 2022 draft. He spent his rookie contract with the Dolphins. Last season, Conner caught nine passes for 91 yards with the Dolphins. Stoll played for the Eagles from 2021 through 2024. He started four games last season with the Saints, catching six passes for 46 yards. During his career, Stoll has 32 starts. At his size and with his experience, Stoll probably has the best shot to make the roster. Kyle’s update, 3:53 p.m. PT: The 49ers signed Stoll to the practice squad, per Mike Garafolo . Ogunjobi is a name just about everybody should know. He’s been in the NFL since 2017. The 32-year-old most recently played for the Bills in 2025. Ogunjobi, 6’3″, 305 pounds, had five tackles for loss last season. If the 32-year-old has anything left in the tank, the Niners will bring him in. Ekuale, 6’3″, 300 pounds, is also 32. His experience pales in comparison to Ogunjobi’s. Ekuale started 16 games for the Patriots in 2024. He has not started more than four games in any other season since entering the NFL in 2019. Ekuale was with the Steelers last year.

summary: The San Francisco 49ers announced they have promoted tight end Brayden Willis to the active roster. He is expected to replace Jake Tonges. Needing an Alfred Collins replacement, the team signed defensive tackle McKinnley Jackson to the practice squad. Jackson, listed at 6’2”, 330 pounds, was drafted by the Bengals in the third round of […]
full_text: Photo by Ian Johnson/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers announced they have promoted tight end Brayden Willis to the active roster. He is expected to replace Jake Tonges. Needing an Alfred Collins replacement, the team signed defensive tackle McKinnley Jackson to the practice squad. Jackson, listed at 6’2”, 330 pounds, was drafted by the Bengals in the third round of the 2024 NFL Draft. He’s appeared in 22 games, including nine a season ago. This is unlikely to be the last move the 49ers make before returning to practice Wednesday, as the team will likely place De’Zhaun Stribling on Injured Reserve and decide what to do with Tonges’s roster spot. As for Jackson, he came on late in the preseason for the Bengals, but was unlikely to crack their 2-deep. Jackson flashed toward the end of his rookie season for the Bengals, recording a tackle for loss in three of the final four games, as well as a sack. He didn’t generate much pressure, but that’s to be expected of a player of that stature. The 49ers are looking for a defensive tackle who can hold their ground against the run. Jackson has the size to do it.

title: 3 final numbers to take away from the 49ers’ win over the Rams
summary: The San Francisco 49ers started the year off with a convincing win over the Los Angeles Rams last Thursday and have their sights set on a 2-0 start with a win over the Miami Dolphins at Levi’s Stadium on Sunday afternoon. Week 1 games can set the tone for a season or be a full-on […]
full_text: (Photo by Quinn Rooney/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers started the year off with a convincing win over the Los Angeles Rams last Thursday and have their sights set on a 2-0 start with a win over the Miami Dolphins at Levi’s Stadium on Sunday afternoon. Week 1 games can set the tone for a season or be a full-on mirage. Deciphering which trends mean something and which can go out the window is an interesting exercise. No matter where you land on the debate, the one thing you always want to be after Week 1 is 1-0. Here are three final numbers to consider from Thursday night’s win: Are the 49ers shifting to more under center formations? According to SumerSports, under center in the NFL saw a sizable increase from 2025 in Week 1, with a 42% UC rate versus 29.2% in 2025. The result? A 32.2% dropback rate from under center is a big jump from 14.6% in 2025, and the UC EPA/DB is up to 0.149, up from 0.103 in 2025. As far as the 49ers go, the offense was under center 57.8% of the time, which is good for 0.20 UC/EPA. Overall, the 49ers’ offensive success rate was 56.2%, rising to 58.3% in late. The 58.3% matches the 49ers’ success rate on dropbacks. The overall offensive EPA sits at 0.17, but the real development could be playing more under center. The 49ers pressure packages The 49ers finished without a sack, but the pass rush and blitz packages were felt on Thursday night. With 14 pressures, seven hurries, and seven QB hits, the 49ers got pressure on 37.5% of the Rams’ dropbacks. Nick Bosa returned and was excellent, but the additions of Osa Odighizuwa and Raheem Morris as defensive coordinator paid instant dividends for a pass rush that was non-existent last season. Predicting a better pass rush wasn’t bold given how poor it was last year, but the sacks will come, and as long as the team continues to disrupt at this level, there will be plenty to go around for the 49ers defensive line. The 49ers offensive line success continues? Speaking of no sacks allowed, the 49ers offensive line was great and allowed pressures on 25% of Purdy’s dropbacks. In fact, the Rams generated “quick pressure” on only 5.7% of the 49ers’ dropbacks. A game plan mixed with quick throws helps, but the offensive line was dominant at times and gave the Rams’ defensive line fits. Here’s to this continuing and finding out whether the Rams’ defensive line was gassed and Myles Garrett was injured, or if the offensive line is taking a stride forward as pass protectors.

title: How 8 former 49ers fared in their Week 1 debuts with their new teams
summary: None of the San Francisco 49ers from a year ago signed lucrative deals like in years past. In fact, most are role players, with only a couple of starters. Still, we’ll track how former 49ers performed throughout the year. There’s no better week to do it than Week 1, when overreactions are rampant. Jauan Jennings […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 13: Kendrick Bourne #17 of the Arizona Cardinals warms up before kickoff against the Los Angeles Chargers during an NFL football game at SoFi Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images None of the San Francisco 49ers from a year ago signed lucrative deals like in years past. In fact, most are role players, with only a couple of starters. Still, we’ll track how former 49ers performed throughout the year. There’s no better week to do it than Week 1, when overreactions are rampant. Jauan Jennings Jennings played 27 passing snaps in his Vikings debut. He was only targeted once across 19 routes. The target came 30 yards downfield. In terms of usage, Jennings ran 68.4% of his routes from the slot. Jennings’ presence was felt in the running game: New Vikings WR Jauan Jennings (14) had 0 catches Sunday on 1 target, but he showed the blocking skills coaches have been talking about on Aaron Jones' TD run. Picture perfect seal of Packers DE Barryn Sorrell (99). pic.twitter.com/fSl6q2qORa — Kevin Seifert (@SeifertESPN) September 14, 2026 Kendrick Bourne Bourne was heavily involved in the Cardinals’ passing attack. Bourne had a higher target share than Mike Evans. He caught all eight targets for 75 yards and had three impact plays, but his average depth of target was five yards. He totaled 40 air yards. He did hold onto his one contested catch and consistently moved the chains for Arizona. Bourne felt like Jacoby Brissett’s security blanket, being in the right place at the right time for his quarterback. Good for Bourne. Spencer Burford Burford starts at left guard for the Raiders. Burford allowed four pressures in 31 pass-blocking snaps. But that makes it sound like he had a bad game, and he didn’t. I watched most of that game, and the Raiders were running wild against the Dolphins. They had 10 rushes for 65 yards behind Burford. He had one clip where he pancaked his defender after moving him a gap over. Remember, it’s essentially Burford’s second season playing the position. I’ll be rooting for him. Brian Robinson Robinson played 18 snaps in his Falcons debut. He’s also Atlanta’s kickoff returner. Robinson returned a kick for 40 yards to begin the third quarter. He had multiple carries in the first quarter. Despite gaining seven and 14 yards on individual carries, Robinson finished the day with 9 total carries for 31 yards. He had a success rate of 33.3% (you want to be in the 40s), with a -1.39 rushing EPA. In fairness to Robinson, his longest run came when he was hit in the backfield. Robinson bounced off the tackle and picked up 14 yards. Three of his runs gained no yards or were losses. Jordan Elliott The 49ers started Elliott and Kalia Davis in 2025. Davis is currently on the Browns’ injured reserve. Elliott played 20 snaps for Robert Saleh’s Titans. He recorded two tackles and a run stop. Interestingly enough, Elliott dropped into coverage and was responsible for a reception. Unsurprisingly, Elliott did not generate a pass rush on nine snaps. Rob Beal Beal, now going by Rob, played 29 snaps total. Fourteen of those came on defense, while the rest came across different special teams units. Beal is in the rotation, as he played as early as the first quarter for the Dolphins. His lone tackle came seven yards downfield, where he tackled Ashton Jeanty. Beal did not record any pressure stats. Skyy Moore Moore played 16 snaps with the Packers. They gave him a reverse in the first quarter, but a penalty negated it. Moore is Green Bay’s returner. He had one target. On 4th & 2, Jordan Love missed Moore with 1:31 remaining. The game was likely over, but Moore looked like he had a step on the defender and could’ve scored. Dee Winters Winters played 39 snaps for Dallas in his debut. Like most Dallas defenders, Winters looked lost. He recorded four tackles and a stop, but also allowed all four of his targets to be completed for 40 yards, good for a quarterback rating of 108.3. Winters was the Cowboys’ fourth-lowest-graded defender, per PFF. I thought Dee Winters had the roughest go among the DAL LBs vs NYG. Too complacent taking on blocks, failed to fall back with post-snap motion multiple times, not on the same page with DBs in coverage multiple times. Missed a tackle. Forgettable debut. #Cowboys . — John Owning (@JohnOwning) September 14, 2026

title: Colin Kaepernick has some things to say about Trent Baalke
summary: One of the many stories still incomplete is what happened during Jim Harbaugh’s tenure with the San Francisco 49ers from 2011-2014. The 49ers went to three straight NFC Championship Games and a Super Bowl, riding a ferocious defense and (for two of those championships, anyway) Colin Kaepernick under center. Then it all just disappeared. Harbaugh […]
full_text: (Photo by Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images) | Getty Images One of the many stories still incomplete is what happened during Jim Harbaugh’s tenure with the San Francisco 49ers from 2011-2014. The 49ers went to three straight NFC Championship Games and a Super Bowl, riding a ferocious defense and (for two of those championships, anyway) Colin Kaepernick under center. Then it all just disappeared. Harbaugh mutually parted ways with the 49ers, followed by numerous retirements and releases. Kaepernick stayed with the team until he and the 49ers parted ways when Kyle Shanahan and John Lynch came in as head coach and general manager, respectively. So what happened? As time went on and news bits came out, almost everything pointed to Trent Baalke, Lynch’s predecessor. Reports documented a power struggle between Baalke and Harbaugh. It didn’t help that Baalke had the ear of 49ers owner and CEO Jed York. Kaepernick has an autobiography, “The Perilous Fight,” coming out and has been doing some interviews to promote it. One with The San Francisco Standard’s Scott Ostler has a few nuggets about Kaepernick’s time with the 49ers, but this answer about his interactions with Baalke seems to be something that continues to add to the GM’s marred tenure with the team: I don’t think Trent was a fan of mine before I walked in the door. In part because, from my understanding, Harbaugh stood on the table and was like, “We need to draft him.” I think there was a power struggle, or a sense of toes being stepped on. I know Trent didn’t agree with me playing over Alex. Also, coming off the 2013 season, I had talked to Harbaugh about ways that we could get better, talked about going to the combine with him to look at receivers together, trying to turn over every stone to get over this hump to win a championship. Harbaugh’s like, “I love it, let’s do it.” Then I get a call from Trent. He says, “Hey, you shouldn’t be going to the combine with Harbaugh. You need to call him and tell him you’re not going. Also, don’t tell him we had this conversation.” To me, that kind of encapsulates how he operated. Those kinds of things, I would say, are manipulative tactics. I don’t think they’re beneficial for anybody. I know other players had issues [with Baalke] as well. I don’t view him as a good person. This is the first time, to my recollection, a 49ers player has gone on record about Baalke’s actual GM practices rather than how difficult he is to deal with . The closest we’ve gotten is reports and sources about what’s been going on in the front office. A good example is that during Chip Kelly’s single year as head coach , he wanted to draft now-Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott. Baalke said no—and provided zero reason why. Given that Baalke was fired from the Jacksonville Jaguars during their head coaching search because no candidate wanted to work with him, it suggests this behavior was a pattern, not an isolated incident. Baalke’s draft picks were laughably bad, so his refusal to let anyone help him make decisions is clearly a flex of power, but it could also stem from insecurity, based on what Kaepernick has said. This also checks out with Baalke’s refusal to want to draft a second quarterback after Harbaugh’s staff felt it was time to move on. We’re still waiting for the documentary of just how the 49ers crumbled. It’s well documented that Harbaugh is difficult to deal with, but it’s been made clear that Baalke is just as—if not more—difficult. I’d love just to know how that relationship was managed for four years and what exactly led to all this. Maybe Kaepernick’s biography will pull back the curtain just a bit more.

title: Titans must start Cedric Gray, Anthony Hill at LB in Week 2
summary: The only positive takeaway from the Tennessee Titans’ Week 1 blunder was the performance of rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. The 60th overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft recorded a team-high 16 tackles. The Titans need to start Hill and Cedric Gray at linebacker versus the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. Hill started in […]
full_text: Aug 4, 2026; Nashville, TN, USA; Tennessee Titans linebacker Anthony Hill (53) talks with the media during training camp at Vanderbilt Health Football Center. Mandatory Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The only positive takeaway from the Tennessee Titans’ Week 1 blunder was the performance of rookie linebacker Anthony Hill Jr. The 60th overall selection in the 2026 NFL Draft recorded a team-high 16 tackles. The Titans need to start Hill and Cedric Gray at linebacker versus the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 2. Hill started in place of Gray, who failed to clear concussion protocol in time for Week 1 after suffering an off-field leisure accident . That put Hill in the starting lineup next to veteran Cody Barton. The rookie took full advantage of the opportunity. Head coach Robert Saleh confirmed that Gray has already cleared protocol during his Monday press conference. That opens up the possibility for the Titans to start Gray and Hill in Week 2. They must be bold enough to send Barton to the bench, especially versus an athletic Eagles offense. Hill didn’t just register 16 tackles. He appeared to have forced and recovered a fumble in Jets territory when he punched the ball loose from sophomore tight end Mason Taylor. The refs called an incomplete pass on the field, and surprisingly upheld that call once Saleh challenged it. Even with his takeaway confusingly stolen from him, Hill still made impact plays. The former Texas standout had a really nice pass breakup on a peanut-punch, breaking up a pass for a Jets running back on a wheel route. Hill also shoved Geno Smith out of bounds short of the sticks on a third-and-short, forcing a fourth down. The rebuilding Titans are still stacking young talent. They aggressively traded up for Hill, nabbing him with a second-round pick they initially didn’t have. That decision paid immediate dividends in Week 1. The Titans were terrible, but Hill was excellent. Hopefully he starts opposite Gray versus the Eagles in Week 2.

full_text: The Washington Commanders are back at practice, and it’s Dallas Cowboys week. Both teams are coming off disappointing division losses and will be looking to climb out of the NFC East basement. Washington announced several roster moves before today’s practice, including placing LB Jordan Magee (hamstring) on injured reserve , and signing veteran iOL Lucas Patrick . Dan Quinn said Tyler Owens will practice today after injuring his ankle during a return on Sunday. LB Frankie Luvu ( groin ) and TE Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) were also injured on Sunday, and won’t practice today. Quinn said there’s some uncertainty on their availability vs the Cowboys, and they would know more later in the week. Quinn said Mike Sainristil’s play was unacceptable after multiple mental mistakes led to Eagles’ scores. He focused on fixing those mistakes today, and said he still has a lot of confidence in the third-year corner, and said he’ll be leveling up. Fans waiting for Trey Amos to return from injured reserve to replace Sainristil in the lineup might have to wait longer than they want. Amos broke his fibula last October, and then suffered an ankle injury to the same leg after he returned during training camp. Quinn said that even after the four-game minimum games missed for going on IR he would still need to practice and ramp up for a return to the field. summary: Jalen Hurts’ 22-yard scramble on a key 3rd-and-18 was impactful in Philadelphia’s 24-22 victory over the Washington Commanders. It was longer lasting for Washington than just one game. full_text: Jalen Hurts’ 22-yard scramble on a key 3rd-and-18 was impactful in Philadelphia’s 24-22 victory over the Washington Commanders. It was longer lasting for Washington than just one game. Linebacker Jordan Magee got hurt on that play, suffering a hamstring strain that will keep him out for some time. The Commanders placed him on injured reserve on Wednesday afternoon, meaning he’ll miss at least for games while recovering from the ailment. Perhaps the play of the game. 3rd & 18 and Jalen Hurts converts for 22 yds. Cannot happen. pic.twitter.com/OuxYeiVaTT — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) September 14, 2026 The previously reported Lucas Patrick signing was the corresponding move. While Magee is the fourth linebacker in Washington’s deep position group, his loss remains a blow on defense and special teams. This loss is magnified by Frankie Luvu’s own hamstring issue. His injury will keep him out of Wednesday’s practice and his status for Week 2 at Dallas is up in the air. Sonny Styles and Leo Chenal are the top healthy linebackers, with Kain Medrano as a reserve on the active roster. The Commanders also have Ale Kaho and Austin Keys on the practice squad . Washington could activate one of those two without having to alter the 53-man roster for the Cowboys game.
